summary: Make sure you have a low profile (LP) slot
reviewText_clean: If you need a low profile, serial adapter for a desktop computer, this 9 Pin Serial Male to 10 Pin Motherboard Header card from StarTech is a solid and inexpensive choice. IMPORTANT: This is for a low profile (LP) slot. If you have a standard profile slot, here is what you need.  StarTech.com 16 Inch (40cm) 9 P Inch Serial Male to 10 P Inch Motherboard Header Slot Plate (PLATE9M16)  Make sure you get the right size for your computer case. This card is mainly for older devices that need a serial port connection but there are still quite a few of them around. I have some older, embroidery card readers and this card worked perfectly for me immediately after installation. Good price and has a lifetime warranty.

summary: Great Sound & Lots Of Features and Uses!
reviewText_clean: I saw something very similar to this in a store chain last year and wanted to purchase it and never did so when I saw this one, I decided it was time. I first off want to say I'm very impressed with this and it was much nicer than I anticipated, even after reading some negatives in reviews. Right out of the box, I was impressed with the weight, look and style of this. The front of it definitely makes it looks vintage and very retro. The cabinet has a nice wood grain look to it and it's just very stylish. I have been having a lot of fun playing with this. One of my main reasons for wanting this was to record songs from my old records, albums and cassettes to MP3's for my iPod so I don't have to pay for and download a lot of the older songs we want. I knew there was a reason I held onto all my cassettes and records for all these years. Now the sound quality turning into MP3 is only going to be as good as what you hear on the cassette or record but that's fine with older music. As far as all the functions work on this (CD player, radio, turntable, cassette, USB port, recording), everything works very well and I have no issues with anything. The sound on this is nice and crisp and clear. With the volume only turned up half way, this is quite loud so there are decent speakers in this. It also comes with a remote for many of the functions. Some you do have to switch and do manually like the arm on turntable since it's not automatic. The remote requires 2 AAA batteries which are not included. The top is hinged well and will stay open unless you close it. There are rubber feet on the bottom so it won't scratch your surfaces that you put this on. The instruction manual is well detailed and I had no issues following it. The digital display displays in red and is easy to read. It does not read and show the radio station numbers and those you need to adjust and find manually by turning the dial. There are no presets for those either. The built in bluetooth allows you to connect your phones or tablet and listen to those through this as well which is a nice feature to have. This system really does have a lot of options for you. You can even connect external speakers if you want more sound and to use in a larger room. Overall, I am very pleased with this and think it's well worth it. I definitely would recommend this. summary: There are better products out there than this
reviewText_clean: Well, it worked flawlessly for ten (10) months of its twenty-four (24) month warranty period, so I gave it two (2) stars. Then, it stopped charging one day. It had to be unplugged to let it reset, and then it started working again. Had the same issue yesterday, and again today. I wrote the company yesterday regarding the two (2) year warranty, and here is the response: "We are sorry to hear that you're having an issue with your charger. The unit appears to be going into fault mode. This can be caused by a number of things: damaged or poor quality cables, a defective device battery, or overloading. Can you please test your cables and devices. Otherwise, because the charger was purchased more than 6 months ago, we will require you to send the unit, preferably in the original packaging, by UPS with prepaid return shipping for inspection and repair to Cargis Power Products. I have provided the shipping details below. Please provide proof of purchase and inform us that you are returning the unit for repair using the email address also provided below so that we can take the necessary action to get you up and running as soon as possible." A two (2) year warranty and they prefer that the unit be returned in the original packaging. lol I buy so many items from Amazon that if I kept the original packaging for the respective warranty periods my house would be full of empty boxes. Not only that, but it would take me an entire day to go through all those boxes to find the right one for the return. Nope, the original packaging goes into recycling the minute I open the item. Then, I have to pay $5+ shipping on a $29 item to have them look it over while I am without a charger. Meanwhile, the devices charge just fine on the Anker vehicle chargers and Anker portable usb hub for my laptop while using the same cords. Think I'll just buy the $29 Anker 10 port charger and call it a day and a lesson learned. Just looking at the websites for the two companies is night and day, but doing a ton of research on $30 items would take up my entire day. Like I said, lesson learned.

summary: ADVICE ON BUYING PROJECTORS + REVIEW - I GIVE THIS UNIT 5 STARS (except for reading online)
reviewText_clean: GET EXTENDED WARRANTY WHEN YOU ADD TO CART Before I begin, let me stress that you should always get an extended warranty with these items. Some projectors will advertise a certain number of hours of use before the lamp stops working, but those estimates are sometimes WAY off. I once had a projector stop working in the first year! Which is fine when you are in the 1 year warranty period, but if it quits shortly thereafter and you don't have an extended, you're out a substantial purchse. I just recently purchased this unit, so I cannot yet vouch for how long it will last, but I purchased a 3 year extended warranty, so I will be covered by that after the original warranty runs out. Now, on to the features! PICTURE QUALITY 720p native resolution gives you a very clear picture. This unit was the best value/price for 720p native resolution. Make sure you look for 1280720 px for 720p native resolution. Many projectors are labeled 1080p but are not 1080p native resoultion (some of them are 480p natively which looks super blurry!). This unit has all the features I needed to get a beautiful picture. You can position the unit near the ceiling and it has a dial in the back that allows you to adjust the angle so you get a symmetrical (even) picture. I chose to place my projector on a small wooden TV tray type table (slightly taller than a coffee table) and was also able to get an even picture after adjusting the dial in the back. BRIGHTNESS (VERY BRIGHT!) AND ADJUSTMENT OPTIONS I have a 150" screen, and the projector was super bright at that distance, even during the day (with the curtains and blinds closed, but with some light leaking through). In fact, it was almost too bright at first and I had to adjust the brightness and contrast. You can choose from several picture modes or adjust it manually. This way you can get a rich or mild picture that's very bright or moderately bright, without having to adjust it manually. I like the manual control as an option, for specific video content (especially live television, which has some shows like Law & Order which are darker, whereas other shows might be overly bright). Connected the unit via HDMI to Comcast X1 and got a beautiful picture, although again it's not 1080p. Still very clear and suits my needs (and budget!). USING WITH ANDROID TV BOX Connected the unit to an android TV box and watched YouTube, played video games, watched movies and shows, and browsed the internet in Google Chrome. LOVED it for all of those uses, EXCEPT going online, as 720p resolution is not ideal for reading text online. USING TO BROWSE INTERNET (NOT HIGHLY RECOMMENDED FOR THIS PARTICULAR USE): NOTE: If you plan to do much online (facebook, reading, Google) and/or use a projector as a primary monitor for a PC, I would recommend getting a 1080p (which is 1920X1080 *native resolution*) or higher projector rather than this unit, but again the price is going to jump so be prepared. For occasional internet browsing, this unit is fine, although text in Chrome isn't always easy to read w/this unit without zooming in (which you can do by pressing CTRL + or -, and then CTRL + 0 to reset the zoom on your browser). SOUND OPTIONS One thing I liked about this unit versus the projector I had before this one is that the volume of the built in speakers can be turned down (off, in my case!) without affecting the output volume of the Audio Out RCA jacks on the back of the unit. In other words, my Sony surround sound system has its own remote, so I was able to use that for the audio and get a big sound & control the volume with the Sony remote... Whereas on another unit I bought, if you tried turning down the built in speakers, it turned down the volume of your stereo, so you were stuck with the built in speakers "always on." This unit does NOT have that problem, thankfully! Was very pleased about that!! :)

summary: Replacement Toshiba laptop battery from Lenoge looks like a winner! (Update after 1 yr. - battery appears to have failed)
reviewText_clean: I needed a replacement battery for my Toshiba laptop, and, while shopping Amazon, I ran across this offering from Lenoge. The specs looked good, and the price was better than an OEM replacement. I've had it now for several months, and it seems to be working fine. It arrived promptly in a protective box and fit my laptop like the original. So far ,,, looks like a winner. BTW, I opened the old battery enclosure following a video on Youtube and found that it contained 18650 Li-Ion batteries which I re-used in a high-power LED flashlight that I also bought from Amazon. Since all of the cells in my old latptop battery enclosure appeared to work individually, I presume that the small electronics package in the battery enclosure was at fault for the extremely poor charging that led me to replace it. Amazon also sells chargers for these batteries like the Revtronic model which I also bought. Note that I was very careful disassembling the battery enclosure and separating the batteries inside to avoid damaging or shorting them. (Update - 26 Oct 2017) Although I have not used my laptop much since I replace the battery with the Lenoge unit, when I taught a course again this past summer, I noticed that the battery was not holding much charge. It looks as if it's getting to about 25% and then stopping. Considering that the original battery lasted 3-4 years and this Lenoge replacement lasted less than one, this is a disappointment. BTW, I tried to find info re any warranty coverage, but without success.

summary: Organize & protect
reviewText_clean: Unfortunately we live in a world that hasn't yet discovered the ultimate solution to the problem we've got with cords. Cords are everywhere, and if you are anything like me this can be really troublesome. I like things to look and be tidy. If you think about everything you use in a day and count the amount of cords you use, you'd be surprised by the number, I think. Prior to ordering this power strip I was using a single surge protector with 6 outlet plugs and NO USB ports. This made things a little complicated as I would have to unplug something every day just to charge my phone. While it does get pretty irritating, I've been doing it for quite some time because it's just something you have to do. I am incredibly happy that I made the decision to buy this surge protector strip. Not only does this have 8 regular outlets, it also includes 5 USB ports and 1 quick charge USB port. Granted, this strip is about twice the size of my older one, but it's also much more useful. I want to mention that this power strip DOES have a grounding plug, which could be a slight issue if you've only got outlets that have two pronged holes. This power strip is awesome, too, because you can turn it off and on when you're not using it. This will come in extremely handy and will certainly save me money...provided I remember to use it! I can turn it off before leaving for work and turn it back on when I get home so I'll be using less electric. I think my favorite thing about this, though, is that I can mount it right on the wall and in some ways it sort of makes everything look a little nicer. I don't particularly love having to move a bunch of wires every time I go to vacuum and I'm sure you don't, either! If you're not completely happy with this product, although I find it hard to believe anyone wouldn't be completely happy with it, there's a little pamphlet included in the package that tells you how to register your item for a limited warranty, which is awesome! This shows me that Aukey is willing to back their product and ensure that the consumer is getting everything they expect/need. After checking this surge protector out I couldn't be more pleased! Would definitely recommend this to anyone looking to clean up the wire clutter a little with a product that can actually save your electronics and a lot of money in the long run! summary: CCA - A Recipe for Disaster
reviewText_clean: The fact that this cable has received 4 out of 5 stars is extremely worrying from a standpoint of assessing Amazon products for purchase via customer reviews. CCA cable is a recipe for disaster for data and voice networks. CCA wire uses an aluminium conductor that is coated with copper. Catergory 6 cable must be complete copper, any cable otherwise will not pass industry standards or third party testing for compliance, and will never certify. For network utilizing POE IEEE802.3af standard, or IEEE802.3at this cable will not stand up to the demands for power and heat. Having not known of this cable before, I bought a box to test on a CCTV project. No sooner was it installed, it started to breakdown. Camera footage became blurry and distorted, and I was extremely unhappy with the performance. The good thing about this cable, is that it took me back to being a firm believer of buying the best cable possible so that I can warranty for building standards 20/25yrs. Reviewers giving this or any CCA product anything more than 1 star are fooling the public and Amazon should swiftly remove their reviews.

summary: sound is so much clearer
reviewText_clean: There are several things that I like about these noise cancelling headphones. They are comfortable. The ear cups on these headphones completely cover my ears. I have small ears but still some headphones that claim to cover the ear don't and hit at all the wrong spots causing major discomfort. These completely encompass my ear and the cushioned rim is soft and plush and sits far enough out in diameter from the ear so as not to press on any nerves or pressure points. Background and ambient noise make it hard for me to understand voices and these do a decent job of removing most of the ambient noise, dimming intrusive sounds making it easier to understand and enjoy what I am listening to whether it is video or audio. The sound is so much clearer. The headphones still work like conventional headphones when the noise cancellation feature is turned off but the difference in the sound, when turned on, is a world of difference. When turned on it seems to amplify the sound and the sound seems more rounded if that makes sense. I could really tell the difference when I used them to listen to some audio files of evp sessions we did on the Queen Mary on vacation. I could hear and identify every little sound. It was impressive. To use the noise cancellation feature you need two AAA batteries which go in the left ear cover. The cover can be removed by sliding it downwards. The cable is 5.9 feet long and it says it is tangle free but I disagree, it does tangle, not as much as regular cables, but it still does tangle some and is really the only thing I didn't like as much. Then again, is there really such a thing as a cable that doesnt tangle? The cable has a noise cancelling mic and there is a multi-function button on the cable that can be used to answer, hang up, switch/swap calls when used with your phone and to play/pause audio. I really like the protective hard-shell carrying case that the headphones came in. It was really handy on my last trip. It holds my headphones on one side with an elastic band, on the opposite side is a small mesh zippered pocket that holds the additional stereo and airline plug adapters. All of the plugs are gold plated. The package also included a 3.1A dual USB car charger. I am happy with these headphones and really happy that they were made here in the USA in California. I also like that they have a 24-month warranty which is unusual for headphones. I purchased my headphones at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

summary: Shockwafe Ultra 9.2 vs. no competition
reviewText_clean: Setup: Bedroom LG OLED65C6P Samsung UBD K8500 When looking for a sound bar, I had a few requirements. 1. It had to have 4K and HDR options 2. It had to have something better than basic Dolby/DTS processing 3. It had to fit the space requirements Initially, I was going to just get a sound bar without surround, but I grew to like the sound from my LG OLED. It wasn't bad. However, my C6P has fantastic 3D, while my home theater tv has crosstalk issues that make it unwatchable to me. This left me having to choose between watching a movie in 3D or watching it with 7.1 surround. So I decided to look for a sound bar with 5.1 to 7.1. Unfortunately, there's not a lot of options in that group that have 4K, HDR, Atmos or DTSX.. Well, there are if you want simulated surround. Originally, I had listed the Nakamichi Shockwafe 7.1 as one of two sound bars I was interested in. So when I started looking again, the Ultra 9.2 was listed... Certainly there was a catch! No, there's no catch. 1000W system, 4K HDR passthrough, Dolby processing and DTS:X. Checked the measurements to be sure I could fit this all in the bedroom... Requirements met! While in transit, I noticed the lack of Atmos/TrueHD and the lack of Dolby Vision. An oversight on my part. Perhaps I'm used to home theater receivers... When I recently bought an Onkyo RZ920, the flagship model, there was no question about HDR, Dolby Vision, Atmos or DTS:X. A flagship audio component should be be just that... The model that does it all, no questions asked. So, when purchasing the Nakamichi Shockwafe Ultra 9.2, I assumed no questions asked. After all, this is Nakamichi, a brand that years back was considered one of the great audiophile brands. Still, having read posts on AVSForum, it appears these things (7.1 TrueHD decoding and Dolby Vision passthrough) can be added via firmware updates, should Nakamichi decide to do so. Not likely though seems to be the general feeling as sound bars take sides in the Dolby vs DTS war. One other thing of note is that this system is intended to have the subwoofers at the rear since the rear speakers also plug into them with RCA plugs. You can place them at the front and run the included cables, but they're about 16ft long. The cables are also about the same thickness of the cable to your phone's wired earbuds. I replaced mine with heavier 25ft RCA cables. No regrets though. Despite the lack of native 7.1 TrueHD or Dolby Vision, I would still be searching for something if I wanted everything. That's just the way sound bars are. Setup was simple enough. Unpack, plug in the HDMI cables and power cords. Connect the rear speakers to the subwoofers (be sure to connect left rears to the left subwoofer and right rears to the right subwoofer) and turn it all on. The subwoofers automatically pair (via bluetooth) to the sound bar. First impressions were not what I expected. I played Guardians of the Galaxy 2 via the LG Netflix app. It seemed muddled. Turns out there were a few things going on, but after tweaking the settings and sitting a little further back, everything was good! My primary movie settings are... DSP: Off (Movie setting adds more bass, but the clarity of the sound gets taken out back) Pure: Off (enables DTS Neural:X processing/upmixing) Bass: 7 (after a lot of testing with Passengers, 6 or 7 seems to be about the highest setting before voices were affected) Treble: 7 (just to match the Bass setting) Center: 10 (helps with the voice clarity) SR: 7 (I noticed almost no change between 1 to 10 while watching movies, but while listening to music, it was night and day) SB: 7 (I noticed almost no change between 1 to 10 while watching movies, but while listening to music, it was night and day) Now, you might be wondering, what do I compare this to. Well, that's not easy or fair to answer... My home theater system is an LG 86UH9500 tv, Onkyo RZ920 receiver, Oppo UDP 203 4k player, with Klipsch Forte speakers (front), Klipsch KSC-C1 (center), Klipsch WB14 speakers (surround), Acoustic Research M1 speakers (rear), and a Velodyne subwoofer. This is like comparing a soccer mom's mini van to a Porsche 911, and thus not a fair comparison. What would be fair though is perhaps to compare to the Logitech Z906 system I have connected to the computer. The Logitech Z906 is a true 5.1 surround system that at full price will cost you $400. Now, the Z906 has flaws. It hasn't been updated in years, and it doesn't have HDMI inputs, so it's not a good option for a home theater setup unless you don't mind using optical/coax and being limited to basic Dolby and DTS processing. Despite all that, used it for years to watch movies on the computer in the bedroom. That being said, if Logitech had ever updated it with HDMI and 4K HDR passthrough, I would have bought that without a second thought since I'm familiar with it. Coming back to the Ultra 9.2, the sound quality is good. I'm not going to spend hours comparing, but with years of the Z906, I'd say the sound quality of the speakers here are just as good, but there's more of them, and they do a lot more with DTS:X and Neural:X supporting it. I've spent a bit of time with it watching the first 2 Hunger Games movies in 4K (as well as testing a bunch of movies while setting up the audio) and I've been pleased with the results. The only real weakness I find is the subwoofers. There's 2 of them, and I expected a lot more room shaking punch. They're really about the same as the subwoofer that comes with the Z906, except they're downward firing while the Logitech is front firing. The impact is right about the same when I gave it the Jurassic Park test. T-Rex won't scare anyone or anything with either. Safe to say, the home theater Velodyne makes things fall down, but again, that's not a fair comparison. I have experienced some odd issues since setting up the Nakamichi. The UHD player sometimes appears to have a stroke and believes it no longer has an HDCP 2.2 connection and reverts to 1080p. Twice now has my TV had a stroke and just starts turning 3D on and off for no reason. And a few times now my Roku 4 picture looks like it was put through a blender and reprocessed in 8bit pixelated gaming Minecraft blocks, and the issue appears to be with HDCP 2.2 going AWOL. The last issue is related to startup. I use a Logitech Harmony remote, and when turning everything on, the Nakamichi input will change as intended, but then it will for no reason decide it wants to be on ARC (HDMI 1) and switch back. This is an issue after starting up, and it doesn't always happen. It seems I need to wait at least 15 seconds before changing the input, otherwise it will always go right back to ARC or won't change at all. I'm hoping this gets worked out with firmware. Lastly, I mentioned a lack of Dolby Vision and 7.1 TrueHD. Dolby Vision isn't on a lot of components. If you happen to have an LG TV and an Oppo player, you can simply use the HDMI audio out of the player to plug into the player, and leave the HDMI video to the TV. In the case of 7.1 TrueHD, you can set your UHD player to PCM instead of bitstream to maintain lossless audio, as suggested on AVSForum. However, you'll want to change it back for DTS:X audio. Personally, I say just leave it on bitstream, and disable Pure mode so that Neural:X can just do its thing. Yes, it's lossy audio then, but I'd be amazed if anyone could tell the difference on a sound bar system. Just the same way 192 bitrate MP3s work fine on your phone with earbuds, but you'll notice it if you play that same MP3 on a high end audio system. So let's end this. The Nakamichi Ultra 9.2 is a one of a kind. It's a real 7.2/9.2 surround system with DTS:X, and 4K HDR passthrough. In the sound bar market, there's nothing else like it. It achieves what it set out to do, and Nakamichi should be proud of it. Yes, there's room for improvement, and I'm sure Nakamichi knows this, but only time will tell what comes next. I would probably give this 4 out of 5 because of the lack of lossless TrueHD and Dolby Vision since this is the flagship, and it is Nakamichi. However, I'm going to let it slide because you can work arounds stated above. There's the issues I've run into as well, but I'm confident firmware updates will resolve it. A few interactions with support have left me feeling Nakamichi really wants to be liked the same way they were long ago. It's under warranty, so I have time if firmware fixes are not an option. For what this is, a 7.2/9.2 sound bar surround system, there's currently no equal.

That's just the way sound bars are. Setup was simple enough. Unpack, plug in the HDMI cables and power cords. Connect the rear speakers to the subwoofers (be sure to connect left rears to the left subwoofer and right rears to the right subwoofer) and turn it all on. The subwoofers automatically pair (via bluetooth) to the sound bar. First impressions were not what I expected. I played Guardians of the Galaxy 2 via the LG Netflix app. It seemed muddled. Turns out there were a few things going on, but after tweaking the settings and sitting a little further back, everything was good! My primary movie settings are... DSP: Off (Movie setting adds more bass, but the clarity of the sound gets taken out back) Pure: Off (enables DTS Neural:X processing/upmixing) Bass: 7 (after a lot of testing with Passengers, 6 or 7 seems to be about the highest setting before voices were affected) Treble: 7 (just to match the Bass setting) Center: 10 (helps with the voice clarity) SR: 7 (I noticed almost no change between 1 to 10 while watching movies, but while listening to music, it was night and day) SB: 7 (I noticed almost no change between 1 to 10 while watching movies, but while listening to music, it was night and day) Now, you might be wondering, what do I compare this to. Well, that's not easy or fair to answer... My home theater system is an LG 86UH9500 tv, Onkyo RZ920 receiver, Oppo UDP 203 4k player, with Klipsch Forte speakers (front), Klipsch KSC-C1 (center), Klipsch WB14 speakers (surround), Acoustic Research M1 speakers (rear), and a Velodyne subwoofer. This is like comparing a soccer mom's mini van to a Porsche 911, and thus not a fair comparison. What would be fair though is perhaps to compare to the Logitech Z906 system I have connected to the computer. The Logitech Z906 is a true 5.1 surround system that at full price will cost you $400. Now, the Z906 has flaws. It hasn't been updated in years, and it doesn't have HDMI inputs, so it's not a good option for a home theater setup unless you don't mind using optical/coax and being limited to basic Dolby and DTS processing. Despite all that, used it for years to watch movies on the computer in the bedroom. That being said, if Logitech had ever updated it with HDMI and 4K HDR passthrough, I would have bought that without a second thought since I'm familiar with it. Coming back to the Ultra 9.2, the sound quality is good. I'm not going to spend hours comparing, but with years of the Z906, I'd say the sound quality of the speakers here are just as good, but there's more of them, and they do a lot more with DTS:X and Neural:X supporting it. I've spent a bit of time with it watching the first 2 Hunger Games movies in 4K (as well as testing a bunch of movies while setting up the audio) and I've been pleased with the results. The only real weakness I find is the subwoofers. There's 2 of them, and I expected a lot more room shaking punch. They're really about the same as the subwoofer that comes with the Z906, except they're downward firing while the Logitech is front firing. The impact is right about the same when I gave it the Jurassic Park test. T-Rex won't scare anyone or anything with either. Safe to say, the home theater Velodyne makes things fall down, but again, that's not a fair comparison. I have experienced some odd issues since setting up the Nakamichi. The UHD player sometimes appears to have a stroke and believes it no longer has an HDCP 2.2 connection and reverts to 1080p. Twice now has my TV had a stroke and just starts turning 3D on and off for no reason. And a few times now my Roku 4 picture looks like it was put through a blender and reprocessed in 8bit pixelated gaming Minecraft blocks, and the issue appears to be with HDCP 2.2 going AWOL. The last issue is related to startup. I use a Logitech Harmony remote, and when turning everything on, the Nakamichi input will change as intended, but then it will for no reason decide it wants to be on ARC (HDMI 1) and switch back. This is an issue after starting up, and it doesn't always happen. It seems I need to wait at least 15 seconds before changing the input, otherwise it will always go right back to ARC or won't change at all. I'm hoping this gets worked out with firmware. Lastly, I mentioned a lack of Dolby Vision and 7.1 TrueHD. Dolby Vision isn't on a lot of components. If you happen to have an LG TV and an Oppo player, you can simply use the HDMI audio out of the player to plug into the player, and leave the HDMI video to the TV. In the case of 7.1 TrueHD, you can set your UHD player to PCM instead of bitstream to maintain lossless audio, as suggested on AVSForum. However, you'll want to change it back for DTS:X audio. Personally, I say just leave it on bitstream, and disable Pure mode so that Neural:X can just do its thing. Yes, it's lossy audio then, but I'd be amazed if anyone could tell the difference on a sound bar system. Just the same way 192 bitrate MP3s work fine on your phone with earbuds, but you'll notice it if you play that same MP3 on a high end audio system. So let's end this. The Nakamichi Ultra 9.2 is a one of a kind. It's a real 7.2/9.2 surround system with DTS:X, and 4K HDR passthrough. In the sound bar market, there's nothing else like it. It achieves what it set out to do, and Nakamichi should be proud of it. Yes, there's room for improvement, and I'm sure Nakamichi knows this, but only time will tell what comes next. I would probably give this 4 out of 5 because of the lack of lossless TrueHD and Dolby Vision since this is the flagship, and it is Nakamichi. However, I'm going to let it slide because you can work arounds stated above. There's the issues I've run into as well, but I'm confident firmware updates will resolve it. A few interactions with support have left me feeling Nakamichi really wants to be liked the same way they were long ago. It's under warranty, so I have time if firmware fixes are not an option. For what this is, a 7.2/9.2 sound bar surround system, there's currently no equal.

reviewText_clean: I loved these when I first got them. The only problem I had at first was that the plug for the micro-usb port didn't seat all the way. I relayed this to a customer service representitive who had contacted me to see what I thought about them, and never received a response. After a few months they stopped taking a charge. Now, I have no problem with this for expensive items, but for a $20 pair of headphones? With how competitve the electronics industry has become most companies I've dealt with will replace an item this inexpensive free of charge when it has a known problem. Some will even request a picture of a the item "destroyed" so they know you aren't scamming them. Since using the warranty on these essentially places them into a higher price bracket they are not a product that I can suggest to anyone. I encourage you to look for something more reliable and with customer service that meets the standard set by todays competitve electronics market. If you are OK to spend $60 on your headphones then search for a nicer pair that these that you won't have to send back to get repaired/replaced. summary: This thing is so loud it will hurt your ears. Mine are ringing just like I left a rock concert.
reviewText_clean: There are two volume settings. One on your blue tooth device such as your phone or tablet, and the other one is this unit itself on the multi-function controller. The controller is waterproof so you can hide your bluetooth cell phone in your pocket, and adjust the levels, and whether you want to skip to the next song, play, pause etc. Yes my ears are still ringing. What I did was turned my cell phones volume up to 10 and then turned this Boss speaker system up to 10. The problem is that when it is really loud like that what you are hearing is extremely loud distorted sound just like a rock concert. That is what makes your ears ring. By backing the volume off on your bluetooth device down to about 6, at least that was the best setting on mine, you get a very clear, clean, undistorted sound that still produces volume levels that are pretty loud. Definitely something you would hear over the roar of an ATV motor. One point I want to make is that I thought the remote for the unit was missing. Then I discovered that there is a compartment at the top that flips up. You press in the black button and everything is in there. The only things in the box are the speaker system, quick start guide, and warranty card. If you buy the  Cobra Electronics Corporation CPP 8000 Cobra JumpPack Charger  you could make this Boss Audio system completely portable for any use. For a weatherproof sound box this thing sounds and performs great. summary: Extremely satisfied with this purchase!
reviewText_clean: These TaoTronics Bluetooth headphones have been an absolute charm! After using a great promo code, I got these for 20 bones, making these a great set of headphones even at its normal doubled price! As an avid lifter (and seldom cardio-er), I wanted a solid-sounding pair of wireless headphones that would stay secure as well as be relatively clandestine while in use. I also wanted it to be easily used while wearing something like a hoodie or hat as well. I am able to do my normal lifts such as bench press without having them slide around, prevent my head from comfortably laying on the bench, etc. During jogging sessions as well as tabata/plyo/sprint sessions, they maintained situated without any issues. The battery life on these headphones is rated at 8 hours, and I find that to be accurate enough. I only need to charge these up with the included micro-USB cable. The cable is relatively short at .5 ft in length. It does, though, charge quickly (~2 hours) from nearly dead to full. The LED light on the headphones turns green when it is fully charged. The mic buttons are located on the right side of the headphones and are easily and intuitive to use. It has all the standard requirements of a wireless set of headphones such as +/- volume, pause, and skip forward or back. It also allows you to take calls and call the previous person you dialed by pressing the multi-function button twice. As for the sound quality, it is definitely more than adequate in terms of volume output and sound clarity. Diving deeper into sound clarity, they are hands-down better than the UA sport wireless heart rate earbuds that go for 200 bones (no joke...). Everything from Rise Against to FFXV, the Inception OST to Dash Berlin, and older songs like No Diggity sound great! Bass lovers will love it as it does have rumble-ier (but messier) bass output akin to the Beats headphones. It also comes with a total of 3 different-sized ear tips. The medium-sized ones come pre-installed and fit my ears well enough. All-in-all, this product looks great (unassuming and slim), sounds very good, and doesn't break the bank. Additionally, Taotronics provides another 6-months to its warranty by making an account and providing the Amazon order number to their database.

summary: Misses the mark by not being designed for real world use
reviewText_clean: My family and I enjoy listening to several SiriusXM programs in our cars. We wanted a way to bring SiriusXM with us beyond the cars and connect to Sirius-ready devices. This radio with nice color display seemed to be just the right thing. Unfortunately, the radio has only what is needed to connect to a stereo - just a stereo mini connector output (no link for SiriusXM Ready radios to interface). Also, the radio warranty becomes void if it gets wet, damp or too humid (so much for using on a boat, or outside on a wet day). Finally, this is another radio and SiriusXM charges an additional fee to activate it (because, of course, you'll be listening to them all at the same time). Suggestion is to save the money on this and download the SiriusXM app for your cell phone.

summary: Hikvision  DS-2CD2032-I in disguise
reviewText_clean: This is rebranded Hikvision 3MP Bullet Camera ( DS-2CD2032-I ), it will accept the current USA firmware for it from Hikvision website , it will not ( or at least I could not ) downgrade the firmware using "whoislooking" 's v5.30 firmware downgrade kit found on IPcamtalk forum. Keep in mind flashing to Hikvision's firmware WILL void the warranty. But I could not the the camera to work using the ONVIF protocol to work with my Hikvision DS 7608 NI E2/8P nvr, hence why I flashed it with the "downgrade kit" , but went up in firmware. Once flashed to the new firmware, you have to activate the camera via Hikvisions SADP software ( I use a laptop, and a Trendnet POE injector and 2 patch cables ),. I also did not enable DHCP, set the IP manually and set the IPv4 Gateway to that of my NVR. Then you plug it in to a POE port of your NVR. When you add the camera, it must be done manually since the NVR ( mine did ) will assume a weak password automatically, the current firmware will accept a strong password to activate. It did take several reboots of the NVR to finally get the camera online. Then you can login to the camera ( assuming your NVR allows for this ) to change the settings in the camera. All my management of my cameras is done via web browser through the NVR and not direct from the NVR , since my NVR is remotely located. The camera has a good picture, a semi wide field of view with the 4mm lens ( good for front door applications ).It supports recording in 3mp mode ( 2048 x 1536 ) . You have a lot of control over the camera once logged into it , with a lot of settings. Some people complain about the image in darkness. I have a front door light, so mine is always in color at night. But with the light off, I get a bit of IR light bouncing off the stucco wall to help, though past 15 feet the image gets dark. My other cameras ( Hikvision DS 2CD263F-1 ) by comparison throw much farther and have a really good night picture, with some noise. The mount is sturdy. I manged to mount to a 4" round bell box plastic blank and then mount that to a 4" round bell box. You can mount it direct, but you'll need a 1" hole to fit the bulky ethernet connector to, as there is no room in the base. This leaves a small bit of room for the 3 screws used to secure the camera. This works if you are mounting the on a wood soffit overhang where were has been pre run back to the NVR, but in stucco you might blow out to much plaster since the 3 holes will be close to the 1 inch hole you need to stuff the ethernet connector. The camera does run a bit warm, but not hot. My other cameras ( Hikvision DS 2CD263F-1 ) run cool by comparison. I have read this is due to smaller compact size and the 48v interface being close to the rear of the camera. This a good camera for the money, and if you can get it to work with your NVR / system with the supplied Trendnet software, that's great, but it is underneath a Hikvision, which are well known for their great cameras.

summary: Good headphones (for a while...Edited review)
reviewText_clean: Very happy with this purchase. I was worried they would be too big, since I have a very small head, but on the smallest setting, they fit comfortably. I also wear glasses, and am pleased to report that I can wear these headphones all day long at work without getting any pain or discomfort around my ears, and the ear cups are big enough to fit all the way around my ears. Sound quality is great, as expected from Sennheiser. These sound as good as my wired Momentums, and the Bluetooth connection is pretty solid with my Samsung Galaxy Note 4. Very minimal skipping, even when I am on a different floor and several rooms away from the phone (left the phone in my bedroom in a top corner of the house on the second floor, and it stays connected when I am in the kitchen on the first floor and opposite corner of the house). Activating the noise cancelling did not have any noticable degradation in sound quality for me, and it really does block out sounds. I was running the garbage disposal in the kitchen sink while listening to a podcast, and couldn't hear the disposal. I downloaded the CapTune app so that I could further customize the settings. With the app, you can turn off voice notification and other sounds. I turned off all the sounds so that I don't have to hear the voice telling me when devices are connected, or when the battery is low, and also to get rid of the little beeps it makes when you raise or lower the volume using the touch pad on the right ear piece. The touch controls do take some getting used to, and are a bit sensitive, so sometimes I want to skip a track, but end up accidentally pausing it instead. I expect I will get better at it with time, and I really like this feature. Have not had any phone calls while wearing these yet, so can't comment on the phone call quality. Took one star off for superficial reasons - they are not very asthetically pleasing. They only come in one color (black), and the build looks rather cheap, in my opinion. Time will tell if they hold up, or fall apart. For now, these meet all of my qualifications, and I hope they will last. Update (09/11/2017): Well...these didn't really last very long. After 6 or 7 months of perfection, these headphones basically became unusable due to constant crackling when in Bluetooth mode. I contacted Sennheiser customer service, and they suggested that I try unpairing and re-pairing the headphones from my phone (Samsung Galaxy Note 4). This did not help. The Sennheiser rep. said that the crackling problem was probably just because in urban areas there are lots of competing signals, etc. The problem with this explanation is that the headphones worked beautifully for the first several months, and I have not moved to a new area, and the crackling happens no matter where I am, even if I am using them while hiking in a very isolated and rural area. The other problem with this explanation is that my much-less-expensive wireless BlueTooth earbuds ($40 range) work perfectly even when I'm in the city, without any crackling at all. The crackling with the Sennheiser headphones started out of nowhere - there was no incident that could have caused it. The headphones have never been dropped or exposed to water or abused in any way. Very disappointed. Update 11/8/2017: I contacted Sennheiser customer service, and after suggesting a few solutions which did not fix the constant crackling/skipping, I sent them in for warranty repair/replacement. After a couple of weeks, I received a box containing a pair of headphones. There was no note or documentation beyond a small card that said the product was refurbished. So I guess they sent me a refurbished pair as a replacement? There was no explanation, and the return address was the name of a person, so it was unclear where the package even came from. Anyway, just tried out the pair they sent me, and the cracking and skipping seems even worse on this pair than on my original. They are really just unusable. I'm not sure what to do at this point beyond maybe contacting customer service again and seeing if I can just get a refund. I love the sound quality of Senns, but they just do not last long. I previously purchased a pair of Momentum 2.0 (wired), which didn't even last a year before the cord went bad and sound was only coming out of one ear. I think it is time for me to try another brand.

Sound quality is great, as expected from Sennheiser. These sound as good as my wired Momentums, and the Bluetooth connection is pretty solid with my Samsung Galaxy Note 4. Very minimal skipping, even when I am on a different floor and several rooms away from the phone (left the phone in my bedroom in a top corner of the house on the second floor, and it stays connected when I am in the kitchen on the first floor and opposite corner of the house). Activating the noise cancelling did not have any noticable degradation in sound quality for me, and it really does block out sounds. I was running the garbage disposal in the kitchen sink while listening to a podcast, and couldn't hear the disposal. I downloaded the CapTune app so that I could further customize the settings. With the app, you can turn off voice notification and other sounds. I turned off all the sounds so that I don't have to hear the voice telling me when devices are connected, or when the battery is low, and also to get rid of the little beeps it makes when you raise or lower the volume using the touch pad on the right ear piece. The touch controls do take some getting used to, and are a bit sensitive, so sometimes I want to skip a track, but end up accidentally pausing it instead. I expect I will get better at it with time, and I really like this feature. Have not had any phone calls while wearing these yet, so can't comment on the phone call quality. Took one star off for superficial reasons - they are not very asthetically pleasing. They only come in one color (black), and the build looks rather cheap, in my opinion. Time will tell if they hold up, or fall apart. For now, these meet all of my qualifications, and I hope they will last. Update (09/11/2017): Well...these didn't really last very long. After 6 or 7 months of perfection, these headphones basically became unusable due to constant crackling when in Bluetooth mode. I contacted Sennheiser customer service, and they suggested that I try unpairing and re-pairing the headphones from my phone (Samsung Galaxy Note 4). This did not help. The Sennheiser rep. said that the crackling problem was probably just because in urban areas there are lots of competing signals, etc. The problem with this explanation is that the headphones worked beautifully for the first several months, and I have not moved to a new area, and the crackling happens no matter where I am, even if I am using them while hiking in a very isolated and rural area. The other problem with this explanation is that my much-less-expensive wireless BlueTooth earbuds ($40 range) work perfectly even when I'm in the city, without any crackling at all. The crackling with the Sennheiser headphones started out of nowhere - there was no incident that could have caused it. The headphones have never been dropped or exposed to water or abused in any way. Very disappointed. Update 11/8/2017: I contacted Sennheiser customer service, and after suggesting a few solutions which did not fix the constant crackling/skipping, I sent them in for warranty repair/replacement. After a couple of weeks, I received a box containing a pair of headphones. There was no note or documentation beyond a small card that said the product was refurbished. So I guess they sent me a refurbished pair as a replacement? There was no explanation, and the return address was the name of a person, so it was unclear where the package even came from. Anyway, just tried out the pair they sent me, and the cracking and skipping seems even worse on this pair than on my original. They are really just unusable. I'm not sure what to do at this point beyond maybe contacting customer service again and seeing if I can just get a refund. I love the sound quality of Senns, but they just do not last long. I previously purchased a pair of Momentum 2.0 (wired), which didn't even last a year before the cord went bad and sound was only coming out of one ear. I think it is time for me to try another brand.

The fact that it sticks out quite a bit and that it tilts means that this is not going to look like just another picture hanging on the wall. I did have to buy longer screws to attach the bracket to my TV. The bottom of the TV pooched out and I needed the included spacers to enable the brackets to clear it. Plus the TV's threaded inserts were recessed. The nearby hardware store only had hex heads in the size I needed ... turns out that this is no problem. There was plenty of space to fit a socket head over the bolt. My studs were 24 inches apart plus where I wanted the TV was not centered between the studs. I wasn't mounting it over a mantel. Where I mounted it, one corner of the TV had to clear the cabinet of an upright piano when lowered. Modifications. I used a flat aluminum bar to span the studs plus longer to fit under the bracket mounting screws. I did this for both the top and bottom brackets. I drilled two new holes into the Monoprice bracket, undoubtedly voiding any warranty. The new holes are for the studs. I didn't want to drill the holes but If I didn't the bolt heads mounting the aluminum bar to the studs would stick out and prevent the bracket from laying flat against the wall. It took a looooong time to drill those holes. I think I'll go for a titanium bit the next time I want to drill into steel. In addition to those stud screws, I attached the bracket to the wall at the four normal attachment points using wall anchors and bolting through the aluminum bar. The wall anchors were rated at 80 pounds each. The aluminum bar hopefully provides vertical reinforcement. The mounting bracket itself provides stiffness to prevent the wall from bowing out. Overall, though, the mount works.

reviewText_clean: These radios appear to be a very good value for the price. I would have given them 5 stars, but the confusion created by the different companies building different models of radios and accessories is really a detriment. It is unclear where to go for warranty, and which accessories are good and which aren't. I wasted money on a programming cable and two antennas that are not up to the qaulity of the radios. Baofeng.us (now calling themselves Pofung), Btech, Sainsonic are all building "Baofeng" radios and accessories. The Sainsonic programming cable for less than $7 is worthless. The supposedly "Nagoya" 771 15" Antennas for a little over $8 each are not properly tuned to the radios, so they don't perform as well as the factory antennas that come on the Btech radios. Pofung radios are FCC part 90 certified and Btech isnt. All this confusion makes buying these radios and accessories a minefield. Once you have done hours of research to find out the true issues and avoid the minefields of deceitful comments and crappy accessories, these radios are good. Just be prepared to spend a lot of time researching, or just pay more for reputable products.

reviewText_clean: Not the best radio, as they tend to drop connection often even though they are line of sight to the router. Otherwise 5 *. Video is OK, but be aware that the resolution is configurable, and default is not the highest quality. Be sure to check setup. I recommend you use the web interface to configure. Also, if you're using DCS-100 camera software, the 934 is NOT supported. Thanks, D-Link!! Fortunately, if you select a 932 instead, the software will complain but will work. (at least on the 4.0.4 version I downloaded from the UK website. Don't ask ...) One huge issue with any IR camera is how to use it for external monitoring through a window. The IR emitters will reflect, and cause the camera to be inoperable during night operation. The following procedure is a good work-around for this. This should work with ANY camera: Tools required: scissors, black electrical tape, maybe an X-acto knife if you wish. 10 minutes max. 1) Do this work at night, with the cam pointed outdoors through the window as you want it. 2) Cover all the IR LEDs with black tape, using multiple layers as needed to totally suppress any emissions. I recommend covering the focus ring as well, but be sure not to cover the actual lens. You could cover the entire front, and use the X-acto to carefully cut out the lens aperture (the black part), if you want. 3) Do NOT cover the light sensor at top, as you want the camera to switch in the IR filter at night as normal. Also, if your camera has a tiny hole for a Microphone, be sure not to cover that, as well. 4) To test your work, set the camera up as normal and look at it at night. You should see a totally black screen, or at least minimal video that's outside, with no reflection. There should be not artifacts that are from the IR system. 5) Install an el-cheapo IR emitter, at least 6" away from the camera to prevent reflection. Test to make sure you get no reflections. The ones I got came from China via Amazon, at $6 each plus $4 for another transformer to power them. They have 48 IR emitters, many more than the 4 on my D-Link. Should noticeably improve the night picture. 6) No soldering, and your warranty is still intact. Also, you can mount the cameras where they need to be to get the best coverage, and the IR emitters where they need to be to provide the best illumination, These might not be the same place for each!

summary: Very high quality keyboard with nice features and clicky-tactile feel
reviewText_clean: I am a big fan of the classic clicky-tactile keyboards such as those found on the old IBM PC keyboards. My main computer at home still has a Unicomp "buckling spring" keyboard, which is my favorite to type on, but unacceptable if other people are around (those key switches are too noisy for crowded office environments). At my work office, I hated the feel of the generic rubber dome keyboards of the sort that come with practically every computer. I bought a Matias Quiet Pro keyboard, which had the tactile feel and excellent response, but was quiet enough to avoid complaints from coworkers. But the key switches used by Matias seem to have a high failure rate, and I had the first keyboard replaced under warranty, then the second one started to have increasing problems with switches that would not reliable register when pressed, or which would double or triple register when pressed once. Matias seemed unconcerned and actually told me on the phone that these keyboard could only be expected to last about one year! So I dropped the Matias keyboard and looked for a high quality keyboard with mechanical key switches yet a fairly quiet sound level. I settled on this "Das Keyboard 4 Professional Soft Tactile MX Brown" keyboard. It uses the Cherry brand MX Brown series key switches, which are the quieter of the two MX models that have the clicky tactile feel and response ('brown' is the designator of this switch version, and the key switch top and stem are colored brown). At the advice of Das Keyboard (a company in Texas), I also ordered an additional quieting kit from Mechanicalkeyboards.com, which consisted of a bag of clear/white rubber O-rings and a key cap pulling tool. I inserted the O-rings under every key cap, and this cuts the noise of a keystroke by perhaps half, making the overall keyboard even quieter. It is still noisier than the typical generic rubber dome computer keyboard, but it is within reason. This is a very expensive keyboard, so there needs to be performance and physical quality. This is a heavy and solid keyboard, and feels like it is glued down to the desktop when I try to pick it up. The top plate is a heavy thick metal plate with a frosted/matte black anodized finish. The key caps have white lettering, which Das Keyboards says are laser etched; so they are not decals like the cheap keyboards use, and there should be no problem with key cap lettering wearing off. All of the wider keys have mechanical 'bails' underneath, so no matter where you press the kay cap, if moves down smoothly as if you had pressed it dead center. The keyboard also has a very nice 'media center' control panel at it upper right. One key puts the computer to sleep if you press it for a few seconds. Another key toggles sound 'mute' on and off. Three keys act for return-to-start (of a sound file or other sound media), go to end of file, and play/pause toggle. A large volume control knob can be turned from the top or 'rubbed' along its right edge. The keyboard connected to the computer over a USB cable, and the keyboard has two USB pass-through ports on its rear edge just behind the Das Keyboard logo (near the media controls). My one real complaint is that instead of using the traditional legs to tip the rear of the keyboard up to a higher level, this keyboard has a red plastic bar that attaches to the bottom rear of the keyboard using magnets. This just seems kind of dumb, and not an advantage over the conventional way of doing it. Worse, the keyboard actually seems to tilt backwards slightly when the bar is not installed, and is only flat when the bar is installed. To raise the rear for a slight forward slope, as most people are probably used to, you need to put a couple shims of some sort under that bar to make it taller.

Update 7-19-17: constant 'restarting' and 'check sd card' errors. I even tried a new sd card. No difference. Additionally, the proximity sensor stopped working. reviewText_clean: To disclose, I received this for sampling purposes at a reduced or no cost. Accordingly, I am leaving out pricing points as a potential consideration. Also, this was tested for more than three weeks and in both a professional and home environment. Please note beforehand that this is NOT UL listed, or not that I can determine. Were this rated alongside a rated item, I would personally defer to a UL listed item. This review takes that factor out of consideration after noting this here, and figures that this has been noted and attempts to discuss the product. The ISELECTOR 4320J is the 3rd ISELECTOR device I have tried out, and the other two performed really well. That was part of the reason I wanted to see how this fared and also the reason I moved it between work and home. With items like this, I try to remain truly skeptical because a failure from something like this can mean a lot of things, but it normally involves risk and danger. That is why I like these, because their setup optimizes not only use but also testing and determination of whether or not this is functioning properly. On this, you have 5 standard AC outlets (specs will be included below) and 2 USB ports, with the USB ports supplying up to 3.4A total between them. What the 3.4A essentially means is that you can charge a phone and a tablet with the USB plugs at the same time, or a combination of all types of items including action cameras, battery packs, and much more. This was tested to see if it provided the allotted charge and whether or not the "smart" technology worked and it turned off after charging needs were met, and these worked really well during testing. This was checked with a multimeter and a load inducer, which detects the V/A supplied and whether or not current is still going to the device after-the-fact. The AC outlets were tested to determine whether or not they were outputting properly and whether or not each outlet was working the way it identified (on or off). This was done with a V meter to see how much output was provided, and each outlet performed up to spec. I personally like the way this is designed, too, because you can determine what your needs are and not have something receiving power that is not in use. You can tell by look or feel, too, with the button depressing and situating in a noticeable, recessed position. Now, I do wish they would include an indicator of some sort (such as a LED light) and perhaps they can do so in the future. This, however, does not detract from the usefulness of the item currently. The rating on this is 15A, which most of your home outlets are equipped up to, and 4300 joules, which is a good power rating for your needs. Other features I like here is the lengthy cord, which allows you to place it without worrying about limitations, and the overall design, with the seeming pretty nice when noted alongside other comparable items. summary: Inexpensive fast drive w/ reliability issues & good RMA policy
reviewText_clean: This particular drive has technically been discontinued, replaced with a slightly updated model, which may have fixed the issues I'll discuss below, but I am not 100% familiar with SSD technology to know for sure. First, the good: the drive is inexpensive, has a moderately decent amount of storage (more than enough for my needs), and is much faster than a spinning-platter drive (especially laptop 5400RPM drives). When it works, it does its job exceedingly well. I don't game, nor do I get out my stop-watch to time how fast applications open, or the system boots. But it makes me happy when I can restart my system for updates or the like, and be back at the desktop in less than a minute, and have applications open near-instantly. Now, the not-so-good. May 2014: I purchased a drive for myself. February 2015: This very first drive was replaced, as it had just died, no warning (very common in SSDs - no warning). They sent out the new one, and everything was good. Life of personal drive #1: 9 months April 2015: I purchased two of these drives for a client who wanted some computers built. I didn't think much of the return of my personal drive, as I understand things happen. October 2015: Personal drive #2 dies. I'm annoyed, but thankful for the long warranty and get drive #3. Life of personal drive #2: 8 months February 2016: Client driveA #1 dies. NOW I'm worried. I get it replaced, and try to keep the client from getting too upset at having spent money for something that failed, then spent more money for me having to replace it (my labor cost). Life of client driveA #1: 10 months April 2016: Client driveB #1 dies. At this point, I'm super frustrated. This is the fourth drive I've seen fail of this model. Mushkin agrees to upgrade us to a drive in their Striker line, model MKNSSDST240GB for a small charge. Supposedly, the Striker's technology is better than the Chronos, with better speed AND reliability. Client agrees to the cost, and I will install that one once I'm back in town (till then, they're using a good ole spinney HDD). Life of client driveB #1: 12 months June 2016: Personal drive #3 starts to freak out. SMART says that two sectors had to be re-allocated, and there's other scary things in the report as well. I'm submitting an RMA request asking to get the same Striker drive deal as what they did for my client. Life of personal drive #3: 7-8-ish months Part of my decision for Mushkin over some of the other brands was the idea of it being American-made. I'm not exactly patriotic, but I still thought it was a neat idea. Hopefully the Striker drives prove to be more reliable and a better experience.

reviewText_clean: A 3-year warranty does not mean much when the unit does not work right out of the box! How frustrating to have a brand new item right out of the box not work whatsoever! I normally use the NewerTech Voyagers, the NewerTech brand was the first to make and sell this type of bare hard drive docking stations and I am currently using four of them. I think I actually bought one of their first models about 12 years ago. When it comes to hard drive enclosures, I make sure to spend the money and do the technical comparisons to be sure I buy a good quality, safe unit for my precious drives. I was taking a chance in buying an off-brand such a Thermaltake. Between my two MacBook Pros I am running about 35 TB of hard drives and I have been putting together my own external drives for nearly 20 years now. Years ago IDE and now SATA. Well, when I put one of my bare hard drives in the back slot of this dual BlacX Duet nothing happened. Numerous tries and no results, the drive does not spin up. Anyway one hour after opening the BlacX Duet, it was back in the box and the RMA label received. I'm sticking with NewerTech!

summary: Good indoors but needs noise reduction outside
reviewText_clean: I'm kind of in the middle about this product. It works well in a lot of ways but in other ways it could use some tweaks. To begin, it's very cool looking and it's made well enough I didn't notice anything better or worse than what seems to be the standard in electronics today. It connected to my phone easily and all of the parts work as indicated with volume control and speaking clarity etc. And I could hear the person on the other side clearly. But there were a few things that need addressing. First, this works very well if the following conditions are met: 1) you're in a quiet space to begin with, and 2) you are close to your phone. To explain further, I had no problems when setting up and making calls in the house with my phone on the table in front of me. But later, when I made a call and then threw the phone in my purse, I had some connectivity issues. When I took the phone out of the bag and held it in my hand, it was much better. So this headset really needs to be in close proximity to the phone for the entire duration of the call. Also, inside the house, it was fine but when I used it in the car, the person on the other end was getting a lot of background noise that the device was picking up. It doesn't seem to have any noise reduction feature. And one last thing is that it's not too comfortable after an hour or so. I felt some fatigue on the ear and had to remove it. But it does come with different size earbud pieces, which I appreciate since I need the smaller ones. It also has a carry bag and ear hooks or loops as well as the charging cable (micro USB). Charging was no issue. I charged it to full in about 45 minutes, not bad overall, but I don't think it was drained when I started so it'll probably need a little more time if it's completely dead. At the end of the day, I will continue to use this product indoors in limited time blocks. But I won't be using it in noisier environments. Read all of the reviews before buying, only because the warranty is kind of unintelligible and I'm not sure that I've understood it to mean that you can return it if you have a problem. Although Amazon would likely allow the return. I received a free or low-cost sample in exchange for my honest review.

summary: RAM Installed & Was Recognized As Promised - Price Was Substantially Less Than Four Crucial Two Gigabyte Modules
reviewText_clean: I've been working on computers since the late 70s and have, needless to say, upgraded a lot of RAM. On this occasion, I replaced four one gigabyte (GB) modules with 2 gigabyte modules. While I normally use Crucial memory, this 8 GB kit was almost fifty dollars cheaper. Since my aging Dell 546 is only worth about $150, I decided to go with a less expensive alternative. The lifetime warranty and service number were also a plus. The modules installed well, although the slots were a bit tighter than I was used to. I suspect this is a function of the slot, not the module. Upon reconnecting power and restarting the computer, the Dell 546 registered all eight gigabytes. According to Microsoft, the new RAM was the same speed as the old RAM. I anticipate better performance since doubling the RAM should negate the need to run a swap file. A swap file allocates space on the hard drive to simulate memory. Since a traditional SATA drive is at least several hundreds of times slower than semi-conductor RAM, not using the swap translates into a substantial increase in speed during periods of high RAM utilization.

summary: Know its limitations and use accordingly
reviewText_clean: I decided to write this review after reading the one where the user lost her TV due to a major surge that came in through the main power lines. I personally use a number of these Tripp Lite units, but do not rely on them as primary protection. The most common surges are caused by in house equipment - my house for example has two sump pumps and a sewage ejector pump, and surges from these pumps travel throughout my house because all circuits are connected at the main breaker panel. In terms of total surge current, these are small surges, and a point of use protector such as this probably does a good job protecting whatever is connected. The bigger, but far more infrequent surges are caused by things like lightning strikes, downed power lines, and other major changes in overall power usage in the grid. These surges can easily exceed the 36 kA/600 joule capacity of this device. That is not what it is designed to protect against. I personally use two levels of protection: a whole house protector, rated at 108 kA at my main load center, and then these at point of use. The whole house protector will protect against major surges originating outside my home, and also internal surges traveling from one circuit inside my house to another. The smaller ones protect against anything that gets past the whole house protector and any surges originating in the same circuit as the appliance. A whole house protector is relatively inexpensive and can be installed by anyone that has some basic experience doing electrical work; if you choose to use an electrician (I didn't), it would cost about an hour of labor at most. You will need two adjacent empty slots in your load center so both 110 V phases are protected. Many very reputable companies (Eaton, Siemens, Cutler Hammer for example) make these. Even with this, I know that I will not be protected against the extremely unlikely occurrence of a direct or very close lightning strike, because that could be several hundred thousand amps and easily exceed the protection capability of any surge protector, but I suppose that is what I pay my home insurance provider for. In summary, use these, but know what they can and cannot do, and plan accordingly. Don't rely on a manufacturer warranty to pay for your fried TV, microwave, or fridge; no surge protector manufacturer makes money from paying out warranty claims. And make sure to also protect your cable and telephone lines - I once lost a TV to a surge that traveled through the coaxial cable.

summary: Be wary - you probably get what you pay for.
reviewText_clean: I ordered this one because it was the cheapest. My Perc 6i was reporting the existing battery as "failed." When I put my first ZTHY replacement in the server didn't detect it, it was reported as "missing" during both boot-up and through OMSA. I left it in overnight to charge and nothing changed. I ordered a replacement and that one had a similar issue...but I got it to work and here is how: I was shutting the server down between replacement, but after the second one failed to be recognized I put my original back in - it showed as "failed" again. Then, with the server still on I unplugged the failed one and plugged the ZTHY back in. Now it showed as "charging." I left it in to go through the charging and learning cycles until it showed through the OMSA in good health. I then shut the server down fully and put my original back in - once again it showed "failed." I then shut the server down fully again and put in the ZTHY and upon boot it was still recognized properly and shows healthy. I'm not sure why I needed to go through this rigmarole - it is possible that the second one took enough of a charge during my first tests that it was recognized on the next insertion and I wouldn't have had to go through this switcheroo. I just hope if it is going to fail it does so before the warranty goes out.

summary: Awesome Amp!!
reviewText_clean: Awesome amp! Sounds great and looks great with full metal chassis. Setup is relatively simple with all the normal adjustment controls you would expect. Speaker and power connectors are all screw compression which is extremely nice and time saving when hooking up. I feel like the red section under he MTX logo should light up though just for aesthetic appeal (or maybe it does and I just can't tell =/ ). But otherwise no external or functionality complaints. Internally is a relatively basic class A/B PCB layout designed well with minimal raised through-hole components. Only raised components are 8 driver transistors for each output FET, but still seem solid enough to not suffer from too much road vibration. The (red) PCB itself appears to be of high-quality with very beefy traces on the power supply side which I really like to see instead of raised bus bars. The only thing that I don't like about this amp is the power supply input & output Shenzhen Acon filter capacitors. Really would have liked to see some Nichicon or Rubycon caps here. Especially for the locked-down $200 price practically everywhere you look for this amp online. I have to take a star down for that because I see these caps in other lower quality amp brands as well and sort of a disappointment. Problem with these Shenzhen market caps is they aren't always the greatest quality. They may work well now but the guarantee 5 years down the road with usual wear and tear is debatable. All-in-all it's a great amp though! Definitely recommend it. Always been a fan of MTX and will continue to be! Just use some slightly more reputable filter caps please. =)

summary: This brand fits the best
reviewText_clean: When I ordered my ipad pro I also ordered several brands of glass screen protectors. All the brands had the same hardness scale & they all had a lifetime warranty. I started out with a different brand. It was okay although I noticed it was about 1.5mm too small around the outer edges. The other brand developed a small chipped area after 1 month. Four months later there was an 8" crack, so much for lasting a lifetime! After removing the "other" brand it was time to try JETech. It is a great fit. The protector goes right up to the edge of the screen. No 1.5mm gap. I was considering switching to the soft vinyl screen protectors after the first tempered glass protector cracked so soon. Then I remembered how difficult it is to apply the vinyl screen protectors without a flaw. I have OCD when it comes to my screen protectors. I cant stand to have a piece of dust in there. The longer you fidget with the protector, the more dust can float in. Lets face it, the application of a rigid glass protector is a lot easier. Also, the bigger the screen gets the harder it is to do a PERFECT application. So, the glass screen protector wins. If you want a perfect fit then choose this brand. I love looking at that big, beautiful, 12.9" retina display through shiny glass instead of a matte vinyl screen protector. The texture is also s-m-o-o-t-h! I love it. NOTE: I was reading some of the reviews & was surprised at some of the 1&2 star ratings due to lack of clean wipes & stickers, etc. Heres a suggestion, how hard is it for you to use an address sticker or TAPE to remove flying dust during application. Also, I always have a bottle of screen cleaning solution along with the "special " cloths. How on Earth do you clean your screens without it? These people actually gave JETech a low rating for not including the supplies with the protector. Maybe JETech assumed people stocked supplies to take care of their equipment. What are you going to do? Wait until your screen is filthy & then go buy the supplies? DUH! Id rather have a lower price & use my own screen cleaning supplies than pay for JETech to include everything but the kitchen sink.

summary: - Not easy to place or tune for motion - Hardware issues ...
reviewText_clean: I initially provided a 4 star review for the Arlo Wire-free product, but I'm dropping my review by 2 stars. Reasons: - Not easy to place or tune for motion - Hardware issues - Decision to use CR123 batteries Each con in long-form: Tuning/Motion-sensing It's not easy or straightforward. You must not approach this with preconceived notions about exactly where you will place the cameras, because it will take some finagling to get working. Once you get past that, and put the cameras where they will perform best, then you'll be good to go. Hardware Issues While the Arlo system has been mostly trouble-free since installation, here I am at 16 months, and I'm in contact with Netgear roughly monthly. Some of the cameras are starting to be problematic-draining batteries, not sensing, not staying connected-and Netgear Support's first comment to me happens to be "With regard to your case, upon registering the camera on our system, it seems that its beyond its hardware warranty. Please be informed that this camera you have has 1 year hardware warranty from the date of purchase which was April 19, 2016." So if the hardware is flaking out at 16 months, and the warranty is a crappy 12 month warranty, that's a bad sign. I seriously expect all of my hardware to be serviceable for 3-5 years, and if all Netgear offers is a garbage 12 month warranty, things are not going well. CR123 Batteries OK, these things are a serious Pain. They are impossible to find, they are expensive, and while they normally last 2-3 months, sometimes they last only weeks. There is a glut of cheap, remanufactured import batteries that have terrible quality, and I have been unable to find a quality rechargeable CR123. So, after letting things stew, my experience with Netgear's Arlo Wirefree product has not been great.
