It is a light laptop for a "gaming" laptop. Battery lasts a good 3-4 hours on high performance under light load, will last double that if settings are adjusted. Detailed review, I am not a gamer per say but am someone who is going back to school online. I need a laptop that works fast and will not get bogged down. I had an Acer Aspire before this and was very happy with it except for the processor. I had some issues with the touchpad that I could not resolve so I sold that pc. I went to upgrade it with a newer model that was a better spec'd unit than the one I replaced. Unfortunately, Acer dropped the backlit keyboard and dvd drive and add poor screen and performance and I returned and was on the look out for a replacement. That is when I found this machine. I consider myself rather tech savvy and while not a "gamer" do enjoy games from time to time. I preface this review with the fact that it does take some technical experience with computers and the ability to read and follow directions. So when I first got the pc I reset it then updated it through Microsoft. Once I spent a few hours updating then the pc screen was flashing and the desktop was unusable. Second try I went to the MSI website and download drivers. Thought since the drivers were date 2015 and I bought this in 2016 almost 2017 that it would already have those drivers installed. So I just installed anything dated 2016. The I look up and read that there is an order to install the drivers. Too late, updated and took forever. I was thinking this machine was bad as it took way longer than my previous Acer. Added one game which took 60gb and decided I wanted the drive for school work. Reset the machine again. Installed all the drivers in the correct order before any updates, then installed updates. WOW what a difference following directions made!! However, I do not think the average user would be able to troubleshoot and figure out what had happened and would just return the pc. The driver update process is really made for tech minded people as there is no GUI like most pc companies i.e. HP, Acer, Dell, etc. So unless you think to update the drivers on your own before you update the pc you will be in trouble. I hope this helps someone if they do buy this pc. So it took me a couple of days to get this laptop set up. There is some bloatware but not too bad in my opinion. There are some MSI bundled programs which can't be removed unless you want to cripple your laptop. Some of them seem rather pointless and redundant and some of them seem rather useful. I just wish I had the option to remove them without reducing functionality so I could really choose if I wanted to keep them or not. All that being said now down to the laptop. This is a really nice budget high spec machine. If you read the specs it looks amazing and really it is. The build quality is not as nice as the previous Acer Aspire I had with some parts like the inner frame of the lcd screen feels loose, the thin aluminum panel used on the top of the laptop where the keyboard also has a little flex and is rough around the edges. The plastic on the bottom is very thin and flexes under medium to slight pressure. The Laptop screen also feels a little loose when opening and closing. However there are a lot of design elements and attention to detail. It seems an attempt was made to hit a lower price point while still offering a pleasing aesthetic. The keyboard and the way it slightly recesses into the laptop make it really comfortable to type. I really do not like the red crest logo on the other side of the screen. Also all of the metal surfaces seem to mark up with fingerprints really fast and no attempts at cleaning really work. The stickers that they put on the laptop also left a lot of residue that left marks on the laptop I can't remove. Not happy about those things. However even with the fingerprint magnet and crest the design is still pleasing to the eye and not overdone. I can take this to meet a client and they don't look at me funny. Now to the specs, The Intel I7 6700HQ processor is now last years news! The skylake chips or 6th gen has been replaced by Kaby lake or 7th gen Intel processors. But wait all the expensive laptops with Kaby lake i7's come with a u model like 7700u. Also because Kaby lake is new the pricing on them is high so the manufacturers have to cut some corners like dvd players or backlit keyboards in order to stay competitive price wise. While the opposite is true for the Skylake processors as manufacturers and sellers know time is limited so they want to sell what they have asap and are discounting most models with a Skylake or earlier. I would recommend you stay away from anything older than skylake for sure so make sure it says 6th gen or number starts with 6. So what's so special about the Intel i7 6700hq? Well it has the 14nm process same as Kaby Lake which means it is more efficient than previous generations and slightly faster. Kaby Lake is clocked higher at the base rate and slightly better optimized for certain uses than Skylake so there really isn't a huge difference in terms of what you would notice. In fact most users would not notice much of a difference if all things were equal between Kaby Lake and Skylake. However the suffix makes a big difference here. U or 7700u means ultra low power processor for maximum power efficiency. The HQ or 6700HQ means quad core. So the base clock is 2.6 on the 6700hq while the base clock on the 7700u is 2.7. They both max out at 3.5 but the 7700u is dual core while the 6700HQ is quad core so in multi core performance the 6700HQ greatly outperforms the 7700u and in single core they are almost identical. So while both processors have the latest manufacturing process and share the same architecture having more core in this instance is a huge factor in performance. Of course mobility takes a hit in terms of battery life but with a decent 6 cell battery and adjusting settings you can get a lot of life out of the quad core processor. Also no computer these days is future proof but the largest thing that affects performance that can't be upgraded is the processor, second graphics card so the i76700HQ is the better choice here. Ram- not really much to say other than 16gb ddr4!! At this price this is very good!! Screen- The screen on this laptop while not being an IPS display is one of the best LCD panels I have ever used on a laptop. The colors are great, the screen is bright even at low settings, viewing angles are excellent for an LCD panel. No touch but really not needed on a laptop. The screen is really nice no corners cut for the cost! Keyboard and mouse- I do not think I will be able to use another keyboard after this. Really. The backlit keyboard is really nice and the keys have a lot of travel and good feel. I can comfortably type a lot which is good because I am a student and writer. The backlighting is adjustable in brightness and should change color although I can't find how to do so. The mouse has buttons which I really like and the synaptics drivers has lots of customizations which are really cool. two finger scrolling does not work as well as single finger edge scrolling. Keyboard and mouse are fantastic! Sound- In a word. Loud. Loudest laptop I have ever owned and the 3d software really works and makes sounds really immersive. For a laptop I am very impressed with the sound. Storage- SSD drive is great and a must have to realize any performance gains from the hardware in this machine. Unfortunately they partitioned the drive and you can't undue it without third party tools which I have no idea if that would void warranty. I am leaving it for now but a gaming laptop should not have a 256gb drive partitioned. Let me partition it if I want to!! Very frustrating. In fact, this and the non intuitive first set up are the only things I can really fault this machine for. Just an FYI. Software- Again there was Norton pre-loaded. Why does anyone pre-load with any anti-virus anymore?? Look at how well MS signature pc's sell even at a higher price because we hate pre-loaded unwanted software!! There was some other bloat but honestly not too much. The other issue is the pre-loaded software you can't remove like SCM, Dragon Center, etc. You can remove them but your laptop won't work right afterwards. Again I don't like to be forced to use any program, specially ones that are redundant just to add value or to act as keyloggers? Not sure but I don't like it. However, there are some interesting features nothing I really need the OS can't do on it's own. MSI and other pc makers try to make your software clean and optimized and forget about adding value through useless programs. Just my 2 cents. Once you remove as much as you can and update drivers and windows it is really fast. Programs load in a snap, install in a snap, run without a problem. The dual fans keep things cool under load and should extend the life of the processor. Some other thoughts. I like the dual fans button to be able to add cooling when you need it is nice and should help keep things running well for longer. I believe there are two slots to upgrade the ram and another hdd bay for future upgrades but you will want to wait until the warranty is over as it will void your warranty plus it is not designed for quick access but rather you have to take the entire bottom panel off for those who like to mod things. Overall for me this is the perfect laptop balance. There are some things I would like a little better but overall for the cost at this time there really isn't a better laptop out there. I like the focus MSI took by providing quality components and cutting minimal corners that if understood the limitations of the machine should hopefully not even be a problem. You would be hard pressed to find a better combination of usable features at even several hundred dollars more. Some sales are listing ddr3, half as much ram and an i5 processor for the cost and of course most will have a standard 5400rpm notebook hdd. At least MSI uses 7200 rpm drives on their analog storage drives. I really don't think you can find a better laptop for the cost. Even if cost is not a consideration it is a really nice machine and has specs I have seen costing at least double. You will find better graphics cards and better build quality if you are willing to spend another $300 or so. For me I will never push this in gaming so the extra cost is not worth it. For what I do this machine is perfect!!

summary: Defective, and years out of warranty when received
reviewText_clean: The dock works fine with the T450s I bought it for, EXCEPT that the audio jack does not work properly. When the dock is plugged in and the laptop removed there is a very strong static buzz through the speakers. After verifying that it is the dock (tried other speakers) and after some Googling I found that a large number of these docks were made with incorrect wiring of the audio jack (poor or no ground). I called Lenovo service about this, but found out that the dock I was sent was years out of warranty so they don't think it's their problem. The only option is to return it and purchase another dock from a third party seller that may have the exact same issue (many people did that and went through two or three without success) or pay the extra hundred dollars or so and get one directly from Lenovo. Is the problem worth $100 to fix? There are two work-arounds for this problem: 1. Plug the speaker cable directly into the laptop. This creates an extra step that must be taken when the laptop is docked/undocked. 2. Turn the speaker power off whenever the laptop is turned off and in the dock, and remember to turn the speakers on when booting the laptop. 3. Use Bluetooth speakers. I'll probably just buy some Bluetooth speakers as it's cheaper than buying the dock from Lenovo.

summary: A Tale of Five Floppy Drives
reviewText_clean: I was trying to recover data from floppies to my Windows 10 Home machine. I ended up trying five different devices and am posting my review to let you know my results. First, all five devices worked PERFECTLY on my Windows 7 Pro laptop. However, when plugging in to my Windows 10 machine, three of them would only sit and spin with the drive light on, even though they were recognized as drives by Win10. After a little looking, I found that the devices that worked on my Windows 10 machine identified themselves and used the driver for the Y-E Data USB floppy, while the devices that just sat and spun identified themselves and used the driver for a TEAC floppy drive. So there must be a little difference in the internal configuration of the drive that is causing the issue. I tried 5 devices and found that the  Tendak USB Floppy Disk Drive  worked perfectly, as did the  Esynic USB Floppy Drive . Both identified as Y-E Data USB floppy drives. When they were plugged in, they worked smoothly and quietly. It was a toss-up which one to choose to keep, but I eventually went with the Tendak because it seemed slightly quieter and faster, but that was really subjective. The Tendak also had more information such as a warranty card and information on how to contact support, while the Esynic box was empty. As far as quality of the drive, they seemed identical. If I had needed more than one drive, I would have kept them both. For me, initially the  Sabrent External USB 1.44 MB 2x Floppy Disk Drive (FL-UDRV)  seemed the nicest. The box was glossy with information covering it, you'd expect to see this sitting on a shelf in a big box store. (All other drives came in plain brown boxes). There were touches of quality in how the drive was packed, the box was made to fit it with a area for the cable to fit in and a dust cover over the USB end to keep it clean. It came with a beautiful guide to using the floppy, including information like the write-protect switch and not removing a floppy while the drive light is on, that newer users would not be familiar with. They also had a support phone number, and the person who answered seemed to be an American. Unfortunately, this was one of the devices that would not work on my Windows 10 machine. It identified as a TEAC USB Floppy drive, and when plugged in it simply had the drive light turn on and continuously seek for data. It worked perfectly in my Windows 7 machine, and was very fast and smooth. The support representative was not aware of any issue that would prevent it from working on my machine, and it does work on other people's Windows 10 machines. If I hadn't needed it working on my Windows 10 machine as well, I would have kept this one in a heartbeat. From other reviews, it appears that it works on other people's Windows 10 machines, so I'd recommend you at least try it. The last two devices were both from Chuanganzhuo.  3.5" USB External Floppy Disk Drive Portable 1.44 MB FDD for PC Windows 2000/XP/Vista/7/8/10,for Mac,No Extra Driver Required,Plug and Play,Black  and the  3.5" USB External Floppy Disk Drive Portable 1.44 MB FDD for PC Windows 2000/XP/Vista/Windows 7/8/10 +Dustproof Scratch-Resistant External Bag Case,No External Driver,Plug and Play . Both devices worked fine on Windows 7 Pro, but on Windows 10 Home they immediately had the drive light up and started a very loud seek process that never finished. These devices were louder than any other drive I tested, but did work just fine under Windows 7. Both used the TEAC USB Floppy driver as well. My conclusion: If you are lucky enough to be one of those whose computers will use the  Sabrent External USB 1.44 MB 2x Floppy Disk Drive (FL-UDRV) , get that drive. It is quality. If you can't, either the  Tendak USB Floppy Disk Drive  or the  Esynic USB Floppy Drive  will probably make you happy.

summary: Good value in easy-to-wear Bluetooth headphones
reviewText_clean: The iClever BoostRun Bluetooth headphones arrived in a nearly-charged condition. (Like most Bluetooth battery-powered accessories the included instructions advise the user to fully charge the device before using it for the first time.) Charging took less than 30 minutes. Pairing was done the same way as other Bluetooth devices, and followed the simple instructions included with the headphones. Pairing was accomplished in one attempt. I normally have trouble fitting in-ear headphones, as the anatomy of my ears is fairly shallow. However, I had no trouble at all inserting and, most importantly, keeping these in my ears. They are lightweight and barely noticeable when being worn. Moving around did not dislodge them. Sound quality: Good, perhaps excellent for the price. I found that using my phone's (Android 6.1) advanced sound settings enhanced the sound from the headphones. The equalizer changes, concert hall reverb, surround sound, etc. all produced noticeable and dramatic improvements. Are these headphones top-of-the-line, Bose quality headphones. No. But then you're not paying $200 to $300 for them as you would for Bose. Why not a five-star rating? I don't know if the claimed stand-by battery life (150 hours) or working time (4.5 hours of conversation) will be proven in extended use. Will update with more experience and add a star if it's accurate. (By the way, remaining battery life is supposed to be available when paired with iOs devices.) Included in the package: ** user manual ** headphones ** micro USB charging cable ** 3 pairs of earbud tips ** warranty card (warranty is 1 year)

reviewText_clean: I've had this case for two years now, and I've been quite happy with it. I use it every day, but usually keep the backlight off. The good: Typing is great, better than some of the newer macbooks. I like good keys, and this keyboard is great for what it is. Very protective, it's taken a few tumbles and been no worse for the wear. Versatility is great, I love that I can disconnect the ipad and turn it around or use it without the keyboard entirely, all while still keeping the ipad cover attached. Battery life is nuts. I think I've charged it 3 times since I got it two years ago. All functions are smooth, easy, and stable... no issues with bluetooth, powering on, wake/sleeping the ipad, or typing. The only lag is when they keyboard wakes up from sleep, but even that is only a second or two. The OK: It's a bit bulky. Even for a protective case, its thicker than most laptops. Depending on your use this could be good or bad It's expensive, though it looks like it has come down in price since I got mine. The Bad: The hinge was really stiff when I got it, however it loosened up over time. But, I discovered this was because the actual mechanism in one of the hinges was unscrewing itself! Because of that, the OTHER hinge had to take all the force of me opening and closing the keyboard multiple times a day, and because of that, all three screws holding it onto the main body of the keyboard wiggled free. This caused that side of the hinge to detach, and made the whole folding unit almost unusable. I'm relatively mechanically inclined, so I was able to pry off the bottom of the keyboard part and figure all of this out, and am now waiting on some new tiny screws to replace the originals that got lost when they came out. At the same time, I'll be able to wrench on the tension nuts on the hinges to both set them to the correct friction on both sides evenly. Also, no reply to my request for a repair cost from their support. So in summary, great case hampered by a shoddily designed hinge. reviewText_clean: Sharx cameras are the best I've seen. Quality of the image is top-notch. Quality of the build is top-notch. The biggest value, however, is the EXCELLENT Tech Support. TIP: Once you have a working configuration, make copies or screen captures of all their software interface pages so you can keep a permanent record. The only area I feel they let me down a little was in not suggesting this when they were on the phone. I read the Manual, later -- and it is mentioned there. But if they are walking you through an installation the night before you are leaving on a lengthy out-of-town trip, you might not have time to read and remember everything. A little suggestion while on the phone (as obvious as it might seem) would have saved days of worry. I cannot really fault them for this because several Techs responded every time I needed help. They have even forwarded to me a replacement LED ring on an older camera that had just passed its Warranty period -- free of charge. Great support, guys!! PLEASE NOTE: No, you cannot Zoom or Pan with these cameras. But most cameras that offer those tricks are either vastly more expensive, or don't work well, or have poor resolution. Another thing I learned from a Pro who installs these systems -- Most people play with the Zoom. Then leave it Zoomed in such a way as to cut off major areas of coverage. Then complain, later, that their Zoomed camera missed all the action. So don't do that if you buy one with that feature! Night Vision on these is mostly not in color. Grass can look like snow. TIP: If you have any difficulty during installation or setup, don't hesitate to contact their Tech Support. These guys seem genuinely eager to help you gain the best experience possible. summary: Case Logic TBC-411 - Quality Compact Backpack for your DSLR and Accessories
reviewText_clean: The  Case Logic Compact Backpack Bags, Indigo (TBC-411)  is a very nice compact backpack that provides all the basic storage for your DSLR and accessories. It has a functional design that works well for storage, transport and active use. This is not as fully functional as a DSLR/computer backpack like the  Case Logic SLRC-206 SLR Camera and 15.4-Inch Laptop Backpack (Black) . And if you really need a heavy hitter, the  Case Logic Kilowatt KSB-102 Large Sling Backpack for Pro DSLR and Laptop  has all the features you would want to transport your gear. But for the quick setup that you need to have ready on the go, this is a very convenient option at a pretty good value. PROS: ++ Dedicated lower DSLR compartment folds down to hold a camera body and attached lens in a ready position ++ Top compartment provides spacious room for an extra lens and a mesh area for extras ++ Padded mesh back panel has cushions for breathability and comfort ++ Attractive synthetic material is tightly stitched for durability ++ Padded Velcro supports can be moved or removed as necessary ++ Includes firm foam throughout for added protection of your gear ++ Slim zippered rear / side compartment fits a tablet (iPad, etc), MacBook Air, or netbook ++ 2 thin zippered side compartments for small / flat accessories and other extras ++ Additional zippered area on the front flap ++ Arm straps are minimal but functional ++ Fabric handle also allows for easy carrying ++ Flat bottom allows the bag to stand on its own ++ Velcro straps allow you to adjust or free camera compartment ++ Extremely lightweight design; total weight is about equal to the gear inside ++ Incredible 25 year quality guarantee CONS: -- No integrated tripod straps -- The camera compartment is too small for longer lenses -- Because of compact size, fits only a limited number of accessories -- No included rain-hood for protection against harsh weather -- Fabric zipper pulls provide limited options for securing them -- Shoulder straps may be too minimal for some; its a minor trade-off given the lightweight design CONCLUSION This bag should not be compared only to full sized DSLR backpacks. This is really meant for on-the-go use, so compared to a day holster or sling it provides much more protection and storage. But if you need more capacity and features, look into one of the other bags recommended above. Having said that, I recommend this bag for its designed purpose. I will definitely be putting it to use. Enjoy.

summary: From 4 stars to 0 -- 6/13/17
reviewText_clean: Not too shabby. It's a good clock radio -- easy to set, attractive, usb charging, and you get a nice night light. I liked the guitar tone for wakeup but the other two wakeup tones were blah, imo. What's up with not having the option to shut off the clock display?? I don't get that, especially in this price range. The bluetooth wakeup feature is hit or miss for me -- sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't...lol! The alarm will default to the guitar tone if bluetooth flakes out. The buttons have good tactile feedback, the unit doesn't feel cheap. Light is handy when I wake up for work in the pitch black wee hours of the morning...looks like an eclipse or something...not a ton of light, but just enough to see what you're doing. Lastly, the sound is not bad and most people will be happy with its sound, but comparing it with other bluetooth speakers -- such as the Bose Soundlink Color -- will reveal its weaknesses as a speaker. Side by side, the JBL sounds brighter than the Bose Color. The Bose definitely has a warmer sound, suitable for all music genres, whereas the JBL can sound tinny and even grating on the high frequencies -- to my ears at least. Dance music sounds a tad richer, more satisfying, on my Bose Color than the Horizon. Don't get me wrong, the Horizon holds its own as far as sound quality, with decent bass response, and if you have nothing to compare the Horizon's sound with, you will love this thing. I recommend it. Update: I've owned this clock radio a tad over 7 months now and was happy with it but now the display is pitch black and unreadable...I just wanted to give potential buyers a heads-up before considering this alarm clock. Stay away from auto-adjust displays, folks. First and last jbl purchase and will look at other clock radios. Update: Contacted tech support in which they told me to press the volume+ and fm buttons simultaneously for three seconds to reset the device. I did that and it did brighten up for a few moments before going back to unreadable in a bright room. What a waste of money. It seems a lot of people are experiencing the same issue with the auto-adjust display being unreadable and it's outrageous that jbl continues to sell a product that is clearly defective -- jbl should give purchasers (who thought they were buying a product that would give them years of dependable use) a refund or a rebate on a future update of this ultimately disappointing product. Here's a pic of my horizon after following jbl's tech-support instructions. The product was working great until this month, when I noticed the clock was progressively getting dimmer and dimmer, until it was impossible to tell what time it was...the lighting in my room hasn't changed so I just think this product is defective junk. Update: Tossed this piece of junk -- which lasted less than 8 months -- back into its box and put in closet and i'm now using the iHome IBN180B which is much more dependable, multiple alarm tones, smaller footprint, has a usb, and a 7-level brightness display you can turn off. I don't miss the Horizon's speaker because I own a Bose speaker that sounds much better. I only bought the jbl because all-in-one devices always interest me...yes, the Horizon does many things, but not particularly well, and fails at being an alarm clock. Update: Contacted JBL regarding the warranty and apparently the seller wasn't an authorized dealer, and my warranty expired by one month -- yeah, right...lol! But they said they will take back the defective unit as a "courtesy" and send a new one. I will then put that sucker straight on eBay, not interested in owning another Horizon...but props to JBL for the courtesy.

summary: Great power supply for cheap!
reviewText_clean: This is a really nice power supply for the price. I got the rm750x. I like the fully module. The 750 watts is more than enough for all my needs. It installed easily. I take comfort in the long warranty. I've known that rm750w (not this rm750x) is a third tier power supply in one of the more popular lists on the internet. That list keeps a tier 1-5 where 1 is superior and 5 is stay away. Tier 3 is pretty good--middle of the road. When I saw that the rm750x was cheaper than the rm750w, I assumed that it too would be middle of the road and didn't give it another thought. But while the rmw series is tier 3, the rmx series is tier 1. This rm750x has gotten a lot of good reviews over the internet. It's a really good power supply for the price and most of the reviews were written when it still had a 7 year warranty and Cosair bumped up the warranty to 10 years! (no registration required either) It installs just like any other power supply I've installed. If you don't have a power supply to remove, you stick it in the power supply spot and tighten 3 or 4 included screws. I had a Antec 300 two that I'm building that I put this in (which is a great budget case if you can find it for $60-$70). The 300 is an ATX case and the power supply fits just fine. The power supply is not meant to fit in a micro or mini case. The cords are all modular and there are plenty of cords. You only plug in the cords you need. You've got your ATX, motherboard, and video card cords which are all sleeved (hides the capacitors in the cords). Then the peripheral cords are all ribbon cords. I would prefer them all sleeved because I think it looks better, but I know some prefer ribbon because they're thinner and easier to hide. It comes with a bag for the extra cords and I store them in an empty drive bay. The included cords are: 20+4 ATX connector 4+4 ATX12V 2 cables with two 6+2 PCI-E video card plugs 4 cables with four 5.25 molex plugs 3 cables with three SATA 5.25 molex to 3.5 converter (floppy drive) power cable to go from the wall to the computer (it also includes install screws and zip ties for neatening up) It's a quiet power supply. It doesn't even spin the fan until it gets warm. And the fan is pretty quiet. The rest of my case fans are definitely noisier than it. It's a rifle bearing fan which is better than a sleeve bearing. Supposedly it will last almost as long as a ball bearing but is quieter. After that, it provides power for my computer. I don't have a lot in there right now. I've got a i5 ATX motherboard, 16GB ram, a test video card (Geforce 6800), two 7200 hard drives and an ssd, two disk drives, and a couple pci express cards. The video card will be changed out soon. I'll be sure to update if I have any issues. But I don't expect any. Seeing it pass with flying colors when tested by online reviews I trust (Jonnyguru, etc). I think Cosair and EVGA and others are going to war for the PC market. This means we're getting some great power supplies for cheap! I'll definitely be using more of these rmx series and will suggest them to clients.

summary: I purchased a GoPro Hero5 Session under some sort of ...
reviewText_clean: I purchased a GoPro Hero5 Session under some sort of Amazon Promotion - $300 for the camera plus a $45 gift card. For those that don't know, at time of purchase, and writing, the camera itself was $300. The back plate was starting to peel off, and the button would slide under the case. The operation of the product was degrading. I sent the camera in for repair under this warranty that I purchased, and over a week later, this is my resolution. 1) First off, they were relatively quick with responding to my request. 2) About 4 days later I received notification that my repair was approved, but would not be repaired by them, it would be sent back to me, I would have to bring it to a local shop, send in the receipt, and then be reimbursed. 3) The following day, I was told that my item was unrepairable, and that I would be receiving a check to settle the warranty. The check was to be for $255, due to a unique way Amazon broke up the deal, which some might argue is fair, I did not. I looked at my purchase as a $300 GoPro with a free $45 gift card. But whatever. 4) I call up, attempting to get them to reimburse the full price of the purchase, to no avail. Through conversation I find out that by settling the warranty with a payout, the warranty is null and void. 5) I was told the reason I was being paid out was that they did not have any replacements in stock. I told them I'd rather wait until they did have a replacement in stock, as this is the only condition that guarantees continuity of warranty. Was told I could not wait. Spoke with a floor supervisor, was told this gem... They DO NOT carry replacement cameras to send back in the event your item is "unrepairable." Every bit of marketing of this plan indicates repair or replacement is possible, but there is absolutely nothing to indicate that they do not replace cameras. They only replace "low end tablets and phones." I imagine that this is their business practice - claim unrepairable, sell the broken or defective products to their depot to be parted out and sold for a profit. Of course, depending on what makes them the most money. This type of marketing is incredibly misleading. If you are purchasing for a camera, please note: this warranty will very likely be a one and done for you, depending on the camera. I don't even know if they repair anything, considering that it was just a back plate in my camera that needed replacement, and they declined to repair that. For all those claiming peace of mind, I suppose this plan does offer you some comfort and protection, but the very misleading nature of the way Amazon markets this warranty means I will never purchase another.

summary: Very happy with this setup
reviewText_clean: ORIGINAL REVIEW: Very happy with this setup. I have had no issues with the unit overheating in my glovebox. The only issue I had was the adhesive failing on my camera mounts. I ended up replacing it with stronger 3M 2 sided tape and they have held up well. The quality is great for a price, and the audio is surprisingly okay. UPDATE: About 10 months after purchasing the camera it started to constantly reboot while driving around. Heat definitely seems to be an issue with this camera. It finally got to the point where after 10-15 hours of driving I would only have 40 minutes of footage. So I contacted SpyTec with about 5 days left in my warranty and they replaced the camera for free. Since the new one is not under warranty, I decided to modify the case and add a fan to it. I trimmed the back cover to still hold the battery in as well which is not seen in these pictures. I have had this new camera running for about 8 months now with no issues with restarting or stopping recording. If anyone is a bit handy and wants to take a shot at modifying theirs with some cooling to improve reliability I would recommend it.

summary: Not accurate, but still an improvement over fitbit-update
reviewText_clean: Update: Product got a software update on 09/02/16 v2.60. Step count is now consistent with LG smartphone app. Product now recognizes that stairs are part of my daily life though count is still not accurate. Step count is consistently low, about 20-25%, so if your goal is 10,000 steps, enter 7500 instead. If your competing against someone with an accurate step counter, such as a 5$ walmart pedometer, you are going to lose. Stairs are a joke. Completely random if stairs will be counted or not. To be fair, the Fitbit, my prior smartwatch, couldn't count stairs either. On the positive side, a super big plus is that it doesn't irritate your wrist. The fitbit was ridiculous. you'd have to switch wrists every other day, no matter how diligent you were about cleaning it, and if you were a slow healer, you would quickly run out of wrists. I don't know why this watch is better. They look about the same, rubber band, plastic body. You can clean this watch much more thoroughly than the fitbit. This watch is waterproof, the fitbit would fry if you got the contacts got wet. I had to get 3 replacements because of this (under warranty). The fourth time was out of warranty and I told them to pound salt. Workmanship seems a lot better, but only time will tell. Does connect consistently and easily with my phone and laptop, which was not a characteristic of the fitbit. Does have some obvious features I had wished the fitbit had. I need to keep my pulse within a certain range when walking to optimize fat burn. The Garmin gives an alert if you leave the zone, the fitbit doesn't have this feature. GPS is plus since you will at least have an accurate distance for your workout, since the step count is worthless. Update: Almost worthless now. Only thing accurate is the time. Steps not even close. Sleep not working at all, though it never worked well. Stairs never worked. I guess accelerometer is fried. Given how much it cost, was hoping for more than 2 years.

summary: Excellent quality magnetic headphones
reviewText_clean: The audio quality is very good with these headphones and they are easy to pair with multiple phones. Noise cancellation is very good compared to the other dedicated bluetooth headsets with mic. The bass is better than any other headphones priced around the same range. The design is perfect to fit around the ears and the magnetic piece on the outside is an excellent design to keep the ear pieces together which reduces damage and it is also easy to prevent them from tangling and twisting. The magnetic piece acts as a necklace and prevents falling off from the neck. The LED indicator and the voice prompt (when hooked into the ears) gives a very good state of the headset while connecting/pairing. The headphone is charged already from the factory, but it's recommended to charge it fully before using it for the first time. I have tried this headphone with my iPhone 6S and also my MacBook Pro and it works well with both of them. The product comes with a one-year worry free warranty.

summary: The Hyper X $80-100 price tag for the same 128GB makes me question how good Kingston thinks their product really is (if that sou
reviewText_clean: When it comes to USB drives, we often time do not think too much about them. They were at one point a mere way to exchange information between rigs, or carry documents with us on a keychain from home to work. As time went on, they evolved in to transferable media styled applications that we can plug into TVs, and use to watch low resolution videos, as well as share pictures from, or use to play music media. The jumps to higher resolutions and larger file sizes brought demand for higher performing devices. The struggle was balancing a reasonable price to what the product has to offer. New standards of USB evolve and release in time, bringing new USB device counterparts to compliment them. The Patriot Supersonic Rage 2 offers a little more than expected after testing, and at half the price of the Kingston Hyper X Savage. After my experience with the Rage 2, it became a no brainer. They can both do the same thing, but the Rage 2 had a little more under the hood (while it did drag in some areas) than the Hyper X. The Hyper X $80-100 price tag for the same 128GB makes me question how good Kingston thinks their product really is (if that sounds challenging, it is meant to). It feels like an alcohol mark up with the Rage 2 being closer in price to a 128GB SSD (and with fairly comparable performance). On the surface the Rage 2 boasts 400/200 Seq Read and Write speeds. Usually in my dealings with Sequential Read/Write speed labeling we see more of a theoretical rounding of the numbers. An OCZ Trion 150 SSD for example, boasts 550R/520W, and this is the top of the 2.5 non NVME Read/Write speeds for an SSD. I have one of these and I clocked it with Crystal Disk more realistically at 490/440. These are still good numbers. Toshiba did not lie about its max capabilities since it is near the ceiling as is, but my point is usually you expect the numbers to be lower, and rounded up for advertising purposes. THAT BEING SAID: The Rage 2 clocked on Crystal Disk @ 402 Read, and an astounding 372 write. This is far greater than as advertised on the sequential write portion, and just above as advertised on the read portion. Now, this is applicable using 3.1 Gen 1. If you attempt to get these speeds via a HUB, over a distance, or in a non 3.1 SS 10/GBs interface you will not achieve this. Cool, so what does this mean for people? If you want a high performing media USB for a reasonably awesome price, the Rage 2 is that. I installed games onto it after formatting it to NTFS, creating a root steam folder, saving the games to it. I experienced low-moderate load times in games (better than my FireCuda SSHD) and now had some of my games OFF PC and on their own well performing, uncluttered drive. This can be useful for you as well if you have a gaming laptop with a 3.1 USB or go to a buddys house and want to port your games with you. Some tweaking of a directory will need to be performed but it is simple and quick. Saving and watching large UHD+ files is easy, and with enough space for some movies it is great for taking with you on flights or trips so that you have a media library on the go. Most of the media should stream off of the USB fine even with 3.0 USB interface. I did a simple heat test with my fingers after playing some games off of it for a while, there was no need to test further after touching it. It was just barely warmer than room temperature Notably warmer but not like oh wow that is getting warm/hot It stayed very cool. Impressive. My Silicon Power 3.0 USB drive heats up like an oven when moving video files back and forth, but the Rage 2 stayed super cool under stress loads. Whatever Patriot did to accomplish this, kudos. While I don't think they used a specific plastic or coating, it is well encapsulated and this may add to assisting in cooling. Idealistically it is designed to complement the 3.1 type A ports if you are looking to do things such as game from USB. Its a neat and fun toy to have and may be perfect for you. If you are someone that just needs a portable drive for small everyday things, save a few extra bucks. This USB is a solid product packed with features (unseen by most not looking) that for the price are pretty stellar. Not all USB drives are created equalor sold equal and it is apparent with what Patriot was able to accomplish here. Where the drives falls behind is the random Read/Write testing. I can honestly say it was fairly predictable that it would. Low random speeds can impact performance, but as far as I was able to determine, nothing noteworthy in real time. Other features of the drive are its compact slider, adding to its self discretion desired by most. The drive has a micro loop to place it on a keychain or lanyard (not included). The small size and look I prefer over the large in your face, overly branded Kingston Hyper X Savage. The cherry on top is a five year warranty that tells me Patriot is confident in the Rage 2, and conveys confidence to me. I will likely outgrow this drive before its end of days are met. I would recommend this drive, if anything I described above is what you are interested in. This type of USB drive is not only super affordable for what it has to offer (even for the every user) but gives the more enthusiastic a fun new device to add to their arsenal. I hope this was somewhat helpful! Good luck!

summary: Solid keyboard overall; thicker profile than expected; keycaps are subpar, but of course replaceable
reviewText_clean: Das Keyboard Review This review is way overdue, which also means I have a lot of experience with this product at this point. Another thing to note is that I don't have much experience with OTHER mechanical keyboards... yet. I was interested in getting a mechanical keyboard for a while, and did a ton of research. The Professional 4 from Das ended up being my first, mainly because of its looks (which I was slightly underwhelmed by; more on this later), and the student discount offered through their official website. Cherry MX Blues ------------- Before purchasing, I got my hands on a key switch sampler. The one thing I wanted most from a mechanical keyboard was what people call tactile feedback. I think I've seen this term used in various ways, some of which I don't agree with. I personally use it to refer to the click that occurs before the key hits the bottom (and apparently you're not supposed to bottom out keys when typing; who knew?). Cherry MX Blues and Greens were the mainstream switches from Cherry which offered this feature (Browns also have them, but it's very faint). And I love these as my first switches in the mechanical keyboard world. They are an absolute joy to type on (I'm using them right now!). I would REALLY like to use these at work as well, but my work environment is pretty quiet, and my coworkers would not be very fond of me if I did so. I have not tried out o-rings, so I can't speak for how much they dampen the sound. These switches also rock for gaming. I wasn't expecting much from the MX Blues gaming experience, considering how much people praise them as typing switches. My first time playing Battlefield 4 with these keys was glorious. It's also easy to subconsciously ignore the click-clacking noise while playing games. My ideal switches would be silent AND have the same clicky feeling as this the Blues. Unfortunately, that's not a thing yet. Apparently the Browns come quite close. MX Clears come closer, but they require more force, which I dislike. Keycaps ------------- Now, I'm not very familiar with all the different mechanical keyboard caps that are available. BUT, I can comment on Das Keyboard's caps, because I have played around on some other keyboards. I vastly prefer the slightly soft touch feel of the caps on Logitech's G710 and WASD Keyboard's CODE. I don't know what that material is called, and how it holds up in the long run though. I have been using this Das Keyboard for several months now, and one thing I noticed is that some of the keys I use more started losing their whiteness very early on. They haven't worn out so far, but definitely darkened in the first few weeks This, I do NOT consider a dealbreaker. One of the major benefits of standard mechanical key switches is that you can buy other sets of keycaps for them. So if you don't like these caps, you can get other, differently colored ones! Rest of Keyboard ------------- I initially picked this keyboard over everything else is the design. The promo images made it look superb. Almost TOO superb, in fact. Don't get me wrong. The keyboard looks fantastic, even compared to many other mechs out there, IMO. But it came with a bit of culture shock. Even after looking at the photos and all on this product listing, and marketing material on the website, I wasn't mentally prepared for how BIG this thing would be. Das Keyboard Professional 4 is built like a tank. The size of Cherry MX (and other mechanical) switches doesn't leave much flexibility for manufacturing slim profile keyboards. This board may look nice from above, but it's pretty thick. Keep this in mind before purchasing this, if you have never used mechanical keyboards before. On the other hand, this thing is very sturdy and stiff. The top is made of some kind of metal, which makes it really heavy, and there is no flex at all. Additionally - and I'm not sure about the loss in ergonomics - I would have preferred if the keys didn't have an overall curvature/dip in them. No, I'm not talking about individual keycaps. The entire array of keys has a slight curve to it. Look at my photos to get a better idea before you buy. The top-down images don't give much perspective on this. Oh, and the media keys are nice. Volume knob is really fun to use. Not as fun as many reviewers make it sound, but it's really nice. Warranty Replacement ------------- When I purchased this keyboard (from the official website, with their student discount), I noticed that the rubber feet on the 'bottom' (closer to user) side of the keyboard didn't hold it in place very well once the red ruler was attached for elevation. One of the feet hovered slightly above my desk. I contacted Das Keyboard about this. They responded quickly, and even shipped a replacement board before asking me to return this one (on request). It was a great experience throughout.

summary: Awesome concept, dead on arrival.
reviewText_clean: Downgrading review since, after multiple attempts over the last month, have been unable to contact the company. On the plus side, the product is well designed, easy to use, mechanically sound, and has a great manual. The effects it can produce are endless. It was well though out. But that's where the greatness ends. There is no mention of a warranty, and no place on their web site, or listed in the manual to get help in case of a problem. My unit, which was a birthday present, arrived with a broken Enter button. Without this button, the unit is nonfunctional. Being an electrical engineer, and getting no support from the vendor, I opened the back of the unit and discovered with an ohm meter there was no conducting pad on the back of the Enter button. I epoxeed a small piece of aluminum foil on the back of the Enter button where the conducting pad should be, and now it works fine. Note: if you go to their website, they list two optional diffusers as being available. These are not available, so plan on only using the diffuser that comes with the product. Unlike the product, the Pixelstick web site is not very good. Lots of fancy pictures, but not a good place to order. Order through Amazon. I wanted to order a pair of special diffusors advertised on the web site to get even more kinds of effects, and there is absolutely no way to order them. They talk about them, and say you can order them, but nope. Maybe this will be fixed soon. It's possible these guys rolled out the product before the web site, support, and manufacturing tests were fully up to speed. I'm rooting for them, but would recommend other photographers hold off buying the Pixelstick until they get their act together. That is, unless you feel lucky, or are desperate, or an electrical engineer handy at fixing things.

summary: OUTSTANDING PICTURE AND SOUND without the outrageous price tag
reviewText_clean: After reading some of the other reviews with a number of issues from lack of brightness to light bleed and dead pixels, I almost feel guilty that I've enjoyed mine for nearly 2 months with flawless performance. My only guess is that the early production runs spit out a few lemons, but that's what the 1yr warranty is for during the "break in" period. Some people would rather write off a model because of a bad unit than have it taken care of and enjoy what really is a GREAT TV. Moving on, I will kick things off by saying that I HIGHLY recommend this model as an excellent choice for picture/sound/features at a price that makes it almost seem like a value model when compared to some of the "high end" (marginally superior) sets from Samsung/Sony. For those who need 3D, you'll want the 8500 series. Besides 3D, the only other difference between this and the 8500 series is greater audio output (20W vs. 40W) on the 8500 model. However, don't let the numbers trick you into believing the sound on the 7700 is "weak" in any way by comparison. Even in a large room, having the volume at around 30% is plenty. The sound, designed by Harmon Kardon, is VASTLY superior to most others out there, thanks to twin downfiring speakers that have decent bass response and remarkable clarity. Is it impressive enough to compete with a home theater speaker system? Of course not, but for casual viewing it's a massive upgrade over the built-in sound of several comparable models. TIP: Ask salesman to connect demo model to in-store WiFi and play a music video on YouTube; better audio test than their stock 4K feed. In regards to the picture quality, it does require some tweaking to achieve the kind of jaw-dropping "WOW" effect that has people jumping to 4K so early in the game. However, there's no shortage of options to help you find just the right setting for your habits. The "smart" setting will match the viewing options to the content type. Example: sports will use the "Sports" preset which will turn on Tru-Motion (aka "soap opera effect") to account for the fast-moving action. The presets do a fair job, but many people have their own viewing preferences that the custom options will help you with. Disney/Pixar Blu-Ray discs come with calibration software that you can use to help fine-tune the image with the TV settings. Keep in mind that while this model gets great praise for it's upscaling from 1080p to 4K, it will not match the quality of native 4K content. Luckily, while we all wait for providers to get to work on building a library, YouTube has a lot of 4K videos to enjoy, and Netflix/Amazon video are the leaders so far. DirecTV has 3 dedicated 4K channels, one that shows sports, one that is a 4K version of their PPV Cinema channel, and the other is typical 4K "documentary" style footage. The inclusion of Dolby Vision puts this model in a league of its own as not all 4K TVs with HDR have that so this model is future proof as more content becomes available. Last but not least is the overall look and styling of this model, which I enjoy. The silver frame is so thin that it almost disappears (especially in a dark room). The TV stand is a simple "boomerang" design but looks very high end. I think the style of this TV really shines when wall-mounted because it's so thin (except where the bottom flares out to accommodate the speakers). The "Magic Remote" is an incredible device, with a microphone for voice command and search, and a "mouse" pointer to make navigation much easier than the typical "arrow keys". There is an extensive LG Content store with an impressive collection of the most sought-after apps, and there is quite a lot of storage space available to load your unit up (depending on what kind of apps you choose). If you already have a smart WiFi Blu-ray player, you may be less inclined to load up the TV with apps, but I've noticed that I tend to prefer having everything I want locally on the TV. Overall, I really think LG did a great job on this model. I've seen impressive models by Samsung and Sony, but honestly the premium price on those provides negligible difference, especially when it comes to the most important aspect: picture quality. I strongly suggest that anyone shopping for a 4K TV check this one out in-store, hopefully viewing more than the stock video source, and judge all others comparably priced against this model. Happy Hunting! **UPDATE** I've had this for ~6 months now and I've still paid attention to what's out there and besides the OLED 4K models or SUPER high end Sony models, I don't think this model can be beat in the "bang for buck" category. I watch a lot of 4K videos on YouTube and I've downloaded a variety of 4K and HDR videos from [...] and stream them from my PC and they're STUNNING! It's a real shame that some people have had some bad luck but the odds that you'd have the same bad luck twice are very slim so if you get a bad one, exchange it for another unit immediately and enjoy what really is an excellent 4K TV!

Cable also supports 4k @ 60Hz, with a lifetime replacement warranty. It is much thicker then my previous cable, and doesn't flex nearly as much. However, you know by the feel that you got a durable cable that will last you quite a long time. Would highly recommend for anyone running above 1080P, regardless of your refresh rate.

summary: A little disappointed
reviewText_clean: I am not thrilled with Windows 10, so some disappointments may be windows. For example, this is a very fast PC but sometimes things grind to a hault and it is almost always Windows 10 is downloading in the background and you are basically forced to reboot b/c everything is annoyingly slow (this doesn't seem to be happening as much anymore though). Really with this fast of a PC? Overall, I am relatively happy with this laptop. My issues are: 1: At about 6 months, the touchpad stopped working. I tried everything. I then resorted to installing the fresh image I created when I first got the laptop to rule out software issues. Still broken. I then got a repair order to ASUS and they repaired it. This sucks though since: You MUST keep your drive in AND they wipe it. So, anything you did POST your fresh image (if you created one) has to be re-done. EVEN WORSE: You are without your NEW laptop for 2 weeks and have to go through the hassle of packing it up and shipping it. Fortunately, t was all covered under warranty including shipping. Well, I am now out of warranty and the touch pad is broken again. I generally use a USB mouse anyway however, there are times where I am sitting somewhere where that doesn't work well but I have no other option now. Pretty disappointing. My previous laptop from another manufacturer had NOTHING break on it for the 8 years I used it. It just got too slow and old... 2: Battery life is pretty bad. I am not even gaming and it only lasts 3-4 hours and feel like I am almost always plugged in. 3: You cannot replace the battery. What happens in 3-4 years when battery life gets even worse? 4: The keyboard is not great. I don't like not having a caps or num lock lights so when I need to use the home and end keys or numbers, I am always guessing which state it is in and I am usually wrong. I just don't like having a power button same size and inline with rest of buttons. I can't type as fast as I would on a regular keyboard (I use a wireless one when I need to do a lot of typing). However, this is true of probably all laptop keyboards. I do not use this for gaming but I might at some point since my son is into gaming. Screen is bright and crisp. I mostly use this for connecting to work, surfing internet, minor photo and video editing and some programming and have been happy with its performance for those tasks. It seems to boot up relatively fast. Would I trust ASUS again? Maybe but I would definitely look at other brands first and weigh my options. The touch pad issue is unacceptable. I'd give this laptop 4-5 stars if it wasn't for the broken touchpad.

reviewText_clean: When you are looking for a security camera and your tech savvy you have a few additional requirements than the normal person. I have to say these cameras are everything I wanted 9 other IP cameras ago and more. 1) Needed to be able to record to my local server -- ex I didn't want to buy some piece of trash NVR when I have a server with terabytes free on it. -- Ubiquity provides FOR FREE their NVR software (which is a dream to use) 2) Needed remote playback AND remote live viewing -- Does this on both android / ios / web browser 3) Configurable alerts / recording zones -- You can configure customized email alerting and multi zone per camera sensitivity (each zone has its own sensitivity) These cameras and the software do all of this and easily. It took me a bit of creativity to run cat5 out to each of them but once that's done you never have to worry about signal interference or how bad the reception is when you run the microwave (something that will drop a wireless camera). If your on the fence just buy one camera, run some cat5 out a window and install the NVR software on a computer to play with. I guarantee you will be sold on the rest.

Update: 08/22/16: I'm not sure why Sony's instruction manual seems to lack information, but like the wireless headphones before them, these actually have 3 different sound modes. One that focuses on sound quality, one that focuses on connection, and another "standard" mode in between. Found out playing with them as I remembered my old Sony MDR ZX770BT headphones had that feature. Just an FYI. Otherwise, had my morning commute with these today. ABSOLUTELY no ear pain. My ears fit completely in the cups. Not partially, not with the lobe being pinched. The sound is awesome. There was 1 track that I tried to use the Xtra Bass feature with and it fit that particular song well, otherwise it is pretty much bass overkill. I ordered the Geekria EJB-0029-06 case to put them away in after seeing a few reviews and how well they seem to fit. Overall still very happy with my purchase of these headphones. Especially at the $100 price tag. Original: 08/21/16 I really wanted a decent sounding pair of BT Headphones, but kept leaning away from them after seeing the negative reviews here on amazon of them breaking and Sony not sticking to the warranty. I decided I would buy them at a dept store that offered their own warranty/replacement service. I started with the MDR-XB650bt because standing in the store they sounded almost the same, at the time they felt comfortable, they had a lower profile, and then there was the $70 price difference. I took those home and used them for my commute the next day. My commute is about an hour long on public Trans, before I could get to work, my ears hurt. The comfort I felt in the store was not long term, I kept wondering what would happen if I forgot to charge them as they did not have the auxiliary input to use them corded. Low and behold, halfway through the day I see that the store had a sale on the 950BT for the same price as the 650's. I went back and exchanged them as soon as I got out of work. They are so much more comfortable. My large ears actually fit fully in the cups, I have my cord in case the battery dies, a replacement plan that is easy to use and I trust, and at a low price point. I haven't been able to get a full days use out of them, but as soon as I do I will update anything worth noting.

summary: BUYER BEWARE -- There is no written warranty or regulator information included with this keyboard.
reviewText_clean: There is a lot wrong with this product, but first the good. It appears to be well constructed and has a nice "feel" to it and the keyboard. However, it does not perform and getting the vendor to respond is a pain. Now for the bad: Buyer Beware: There is no written warranty with the product. In fact, there is no written regulatory or safety documentation. While the vendor says they have an 18-month warranty, no details are provided as to what the vendor warrants. DOA or close enough to it and no actual support from the vendor. I turned the unit on, expecting to have to charge the internal battery and both the power and blue tooth lights lit. However, after a moment, both lights went out, suggesting that I need to charge the unit. I plugged in the keyboard via the supplied USB cable and after about 2.5 hours, the unit showed the green power light, indicating that it was fully charged. I unplugged the unit and placed it near my ipad Air and turned in on. After about a second passed, the green power light went out and less than five seconds later, the bluetooth light went out. I attached the keyboard to the USB cable and recharged it. After a few moments, the power light changed from red to green. Rather than unplug the USB cable, I turned the unit on. The green power light stayed on and the bluetooth light came on. After about five seconds the bluetooth light went out. It was supposed to flash, indicating that it was attempting to seek a bluetooth device and connect to it. The green light was still on, so I unplugged the USB cable. After a second, the power light went out. I detailed this in an email to the vendor and got back a canned response that they were in the process of moving. They provided me with a trouble ticket number and said to put Urgent in the subject line if this was an urgent problem. So I responded and got no response back from that email. The next day, I used the Amazon link to contact the vendor and again detailed my experience. This was the day after the move was supposed to be finished. The response was the same as before -- that they were in the process of moving and they issued another trouble ticket. Then I got a request via Amazon from the vendor to rate my experience with the product. This did not sit well with me, since they have failed to provide anything more than two trouble ticket numbers. My response detailed my experience and the response was the same as the others -- they were in the process of moving and issued yet another trouble ticket number. The problem is that the three ticket numbers are not anywhere approaching sequential, but are all over the place: #9054955, #3941885, and #7510694, in that order. Either they get a lot of trouble tickets, or they are generating the numbers with some kind of random number generator. Regardless, there has been no response from the vendor that even deals with the problem and no attempt to make this right by telling me what needs to be done (even if it is to return the product to Amazon). To say the least, my experience with this vendor is less than ideal. The keyboard itself has a number of reviews expressing failure. In a few cases, the vendor has responded, but in far too many, there has been no response. The other problem is that the keyboard failures are happening at any time, suggesting that this is a really bad product. Normal failure of electronic products occur within the first ninety days, and any failure past that time is very unusual. But given the number of negative responses, any kind of manufacturing quality control must be non-existent or close to it. Now to blue-tooth operation. It is far from the best. I don't want to spend the $100 Apple charges for their keyboard, given the number of complaints I've seen with bluetooth operation in general. Instead, I'm opting for a wired keyboard that is used in classrooms and complete with a builtin stand to hold my ipad. This worthless piece of junk is going to be returned for a refund if I don't hear anything by the end of tomorrow -- it will have been a week with no support responses from the vendor.

summary: Good headphones for certain tastes
reviewText_clean: I bought the Shure SRH144 (the "semi-open" model). I'd call them a quality set of headphones with a lot to admire. They look good, they're foldable, and they manage to be feel well-made, substantial, and light (5.3 oz) all at once. They put just the right amount of pressure on your head -- enough to be secure without feeling tight -- and they don't overheat your ears on long walks, making them comfortable in every way. The two-year warranty is generous, and it's a welcome sight to see bigger-than-average 36mm drivers at this price point (30mm is standard for cheap headphones). The only design detail to complain about is the weirdly bulky headphone jack. As for sound quality, most professional reviews seem to say these sound good (a minority disagree), while the Amazon opinions are more mixed. I'm somewhere in the middle. The best way to describe the sound is probably "accurate" -- the SRH144s reproduce music faithfully and properly. But they also have a flat/neutral bias that seems aimed at purists. It would probably go down well in, say, Japan, but I'm a typical American who likes a tad more bass and treble (not wretched excess bass like Beats headphones, just a little more), and to my ears, these headphones need more punch. You could say I admire these headphones more than I like them, so back to Amazon they go. But if you like your music flat, dive right in. (Note: the SRH145s are supposedly stronger in the bass department than the 144s. Both have been discontinued as of summer 2018.)

summary: Works with 2007 Nissan Frontier and Rockford Fosgate audio, with some caveats
reviewText_clean: For starters, USA SPEC's web site specifically states that if these units are purchased from Amazon, or any online company not Crutchfield, then there is no warranty. For USA SPEC--fix your documentation. Nissan never offered Bose audio as an option for the Nissan Frontier. At least not for the current body style that was created around 2005. The only audio upgrade is Rockford Fosgate (what's in a name; the Rockford Fosgate system is made by Panasonic for Nissan). That said, it works as documented with the Rockford Fosgate audio system. It took me about 20 minutes to install, but I was already familiar with removing my radio and with the connections. The only hard part was getting the new connectors out of the way so the unit will go back in. Hint: move them so that they rest on top of the radio. The cables are idiot proof, so you can't connect them wrong. If you have the Rockford Fosgate system with steering wheel audio controls, know that the steering wheel controls cannot be used at all to change tracks. If you turn off audio with the steering wheel power button, it will stop playing and start again when you turn power on, so that's kinda pause/play. The controls on the radio do work as advertised. Skip back/forward will change tracks, etc. You also get full text display on the radio. The voice prompt setting won't stay turned off, but perhaps that's because the unit I got was from a gray market source? I'll find out since I'm getting one from Crutchfield. I've also had a few problems with connecting to my Pixel 2 XL, but I suspect that's either because of the unapproved supplier, or location of the bluetooth module. Sound quality is fine. Using the satellite input has nothing to do with the sound quality, nor does the fact that this unit impersonates the satellite unit. It is nice having everything mostly integrated, versus a separate bluetooth module that just plugs into my AUX port. I don't and won't likely use this for phone calls, so I have no feedback there. I also already have an AUX port, so probably won't use the one on this product. I'll be cross posting a version of this review on Crutchfield.

summary: Stick to the moto 7420 on cox networks
reviewText_clean: Really wanted to like this product. I'm so sick of the typical motorola/arris products that literally last barely a year then stop working. It seems like I need a new modem at least once a year, or just barely past the warranty period. I've been using the arris modems but after doing my research and finding they actually are not the same product quality that motorola used to make before they bought out or merged with them. I've been a big TP-Link fan for a long time as they have some very reliable and capable router and adapter products I've been very happy with. While the specs on here state it is compatible with COX, I've been told by the cox reps in Phoenix AZ that it is not. They will only support the cheaper and slower TC7610 model , though that may be fine for you. They will also support the tp link 16x4 model with the built in routerwhich I did not want. I did convince them to at least let me try it, since I had it already. They loaded me in the system and registered it as though it was the 7610 model, but it still managed to connect with all 16x4 channels. The speed was ok. Because of the wiring in my older neighborhood I can't get more than 300mpbs up and 30 down. The prior arris modem would usually get about 305/33. The tp link would peak at about 275 during a speed test, then slowly creep up. That tells me that it isn't compatible with the "speed boost" type features that most ISPs use. After a few days of use, the tp link modem would slow to a crawl and need to be rebooted. I can't say for sure if that is a modem issue or a cox issue, but it isn't something I'm willing to live with either way. So, back it goes to amazon, I would have really liked to support TP link with this product but instead I have purchased the MOTOROLA MB7420 . Note this is not an arris model. Anecdotal evidence of my own and many others I've talked to equates any of the arris products with being poor quality, and the white models seem to be even worse coincidentally. Very happy so far with the moto which is performing much better than the tp link did in the exact same setup.

summary: Falling stars...
reviewText_clean: This Bluray player has a gorgeous picture in comparison with the Swansong it replaced (which suddenly went crazy turning the TV on and off). It has a very small footprint, actually smaller than a hardback Harry Potter book. But I do feel Sony pulled a fast one with claiming that it plays all formats of video file, though... It does, in a manner of speaking. It will play MP4's and MKv's all right, but only through a USB stick--forget about streaming anything other than an AVI from a NAS. For that you will need to buy a small (inexpensive) software package that transcodes on the fly, and run it from an external server. It's anybody's guess why Sony can't be bothered to include that ability; but it nearly caused me to send the darn thing back for one that equals the streaming ability other blu ray players (Panasonic, Samsung, etc) ship with as a matter of course. As it is, I had it all set up already when I discovered the shortfall, and I was so impressed with the picture that I searched for and found a workaround ... and I decided to keep it. For that I deduct one star... Everything else works well, although I haven't yet tried playing playstation games on it (as Sony claims I can). Edit 2/8/2017: Eight days after the last day i could have returned it to Amazon, therefore bypassing Sony RMA process.. Yes, of course it quit. I had been watching plain ol' DVD's, and today when I swapped to the last disk in the series, the SONY player shut off and will not restart. At. All. (The cheap little milk frother I bought from Amazon on the same day is still running.) So yeah, I hacked off another two stars--I'll put them back if Sony is able to repair this thing. Edit 2/25/2017: Contacted Sony for technical assist/warranty repair, and they didn't argue or quibble a bit. Issued an RMA#, FEDEx prepaid, with a promise to repair or replace within 7-10 days. Sony was as good as their word, can't fault them on that. I received a brand new unit yesterday. I truly hope that my first experience was a fluke, and that I got a good one this time, because IMO there is NO picture comparison anywhere on the market. It's easy to set up and I really love the video quality. So I am returning the stars--deducting only one for the crap I went through to get back to square one, and the fact that I lost one disc of a brand new multi-disc set (it could not be retrieved from the player without voiding the warranty)..

summary: Almost GREAT
reviewText_clean: We've had two of these entry-level 'audiophile' turntables, and have found NONE of the stability issues dramatized by numerous others. Our first purchase was early in the production run, October, 2015, then we placed it with a friend. Our second purchase was in June, 2016. Because of the negative interim reviews, we ran thorough tests of the motor's performance, including three separate 72-hour continuous tests, then subsequent daily use. No speed or other functional issues whatsoever. The peak of these reported problems appeared to occur between our two purchase cycles. Perhaps TEAC has replaced the motor supplier, or improved its quality control testing. The build quality and choice of materials is excellent. Its tonearm is beautifully cast, controls feel satisfying, its color finish on the plinth is flawless, dust cover/hinges beautifully crafted, even the isolation feet are a thing of beauty. Its A/T cartridge/stylus has also come under criticism. Like the turntable, it's an adequate entry-level combo and it needs to be broken in for about ten hours of play. On newer era pressings, It does a nice job, but we found it's reproduction hit-and-miss on vintage pressings. We're looking forward to upgrading to a Grado or Ortofon and comparing the results. Why 4-Stars? The warranty is only 90-days, and given others' issues, 12-months coverage would instill more confidence in buyers. We have not contacted TEAC customer service.

summary: Forget the Bose.
reviewText_clean: Bought these to replace my PXC 450's I purchased here on Amazon 7 years ago. The 450's fit was excellent. I wore them on 14-17 hour international flights at an average of 10 hours straight with the headphones on and never had a sore ear from the headphone cups. Well the 450's just died and to get them repaired would cost almost half the price of a new pair of headphones. (Be sure to read Sennheiser's warranty) I needed a new pair for a short domestic flight. Yes, I hate being crammed into a little flying capsule with tons of strange people, and worse, having to listen to them. These 550's work awesome. The ear cups felt a bit smaller than the 450's but still had a comfortable fit. I loved the option of bluetooth or (supplied) wire connection. When I travel by myself I sometimes use bluetooth but when I travel with my child we're always plugged into the computer watching movies using a splitter since they currently have wired headphones. Great, great option you won't find on other higher end headphones. I'm no audiophile so hearing those subtle differences are irrelevant to me. I just need to cancel out some noise, enjoy listening to a movie or music, have a fit that won't start bothering me a couple hours later and the nice option of bluetooth or wired. The 550's met all those expectations. The touch controls will need some practice. I recommend practicing before your trip so finding the right spots to touch and slide won't be an issue during your trip. Otherwise you'll be taking off the headphones and putting back on to find the right spots that control different features.
